brief_summary: Eating a Mediterranean-style diet and doing regular resistance training are both known to lower the risk of heart disease. However, most people find it hard to stick to these habits over time, and few smartphone apps support both diet and strength training together. This study tests a smartphone app called MedEx Tracker, which was developed by the research team. The app lets people record what they have eaten against a set of Mediterranean diet targets, record the weight and repetitions for each set of their resistance training, and see how they are doing through a progress screen. It also sends reminders during the day and suggests when to increase training weight. Healthy adults aged 18 to 55 will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will be given the same Mediterranean diet targets and the same strength training programme. One group will receive this through the app; the other will receive it as a printed booklet. This means any difference between the groups should be due to the app itself rather than to different advice. Everyone will attend the laboratory before and after the four weeks for measurements and questionnaires. The main aim is to find out whether the app is usable and acceptable to participants, and whether it helps people stick to a Mediterranean-style diet and a resistance training programme. The findings will be used to decide whether the app is suitable for a larger future study.
interventions: Printed dietary and resistance exercise programme
title: Testing a Smartphone App to Support a Mediterranean Diet and Strength Exercise

brief_summary: After some operations in which tissue is removed, it is necessary to repair the defect with a piece of tissue from another location in the body. This is called a microsurgically transplanted tissue flap (or tissue flap, for short). It is important that, after an operation, enough blood flows to the relocated tissue. In this study, we want to investigate whether, after the operation, measuring oxygen in the tissue flap with the INVOS 7100c device helps detect blood flow problems earlier. In the future, this could help doctors intervene more quickly, thereby reducing the risk of complications.
title: Flap Assessment With Regional Oximetry for Early Detection of Compromise in Free Flap Reconstructive Surgery - FLARE Study

brief_summary: This retrospective, multicenter, observational study will evaluate an artificial intelligence-based system for quantitative assessment and risk stratification of coronary atherosclerotic plaque. Adults with coronary plaque on baseline coronary CT angiography (CCTA) and at least one follow-up CCTA obtained between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2025 will be identified from participating centers. The system will integrate clinical factors, CCTA plaque morphology and burden, functional measures, hemodynamic parameters, and biomechanical features using baseline data. Two independent readers will assess conventional CCTA findings, including CAD-RADS and adverse plaque characteristics, while remaining blinded to system outputs. The primary outcome is patient-level definite progression of non-calcified plaque, defined by annualized change in non-calcified plaque percent atheroma volume exceeding the reproducibility-based minimum detectable change (MDC95). Model discrimination will be assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and compared with conventional CCTA models. Approximately 326 participants are planned.
primary_outcomes: Patient-level definite non-calcified plaque progression discrimination (AUC)
title: AI-Based CT Analysis of Coronary Plaque Evolution

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study iMMagine-4 is to compare and assess the safety and effectiveness of anitocabtagene autoleucel versus standard of care therapy (SOCT) in participants with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) who are not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant.

The primary objective of this study is to compare the efficacy of anitocabtagene autoleucel versus quadruplet-based SOCT in participants with NDMM who are not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant (auto-SCT).
primary_outcomes: Minimal Residual Disease (MRD)-Negative Complete Response (CR) or Stringent CR (sCR) Rate at 12 Months
title: A Trial to Evaluate Safety and Efficacy of Anitocabtagene Autoleucel Versus Standard of Care in Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary: The effect of probiotics on skin health in healthy women with dry to very dry facial skin.
title: Effects of Probiotics on Skin Health in Healthy Women

brief_summary:
Severe obesity is a chronic condition that can lead to a range of serious health problems. One common treatment option is sleeve gastrectomy, a weight-loss operation in which the size of the stomach is reduced. These procedures are increasingly being performed with the support of robotic surgical systems. However, there is still limited clinical experience with the Hugo™ Robotic-Assisted Surgery System for this type of operation.

The aim of this study is to evaluate whether sleeve gastrectomy can be performed safely and reliably using the Hugo™ system. In particular, the study will assess whether the operation can be completed as planned with the robotic system and will examine outcomes during and after surgery.

The study will include 50 adults with severe obesity who are scheduled to undergo sleeve gastrectomy. Information will be collected during the operation, including the duration of different surgical steps and the occurrence of any complications. Participants will be followed for six months after surgery. During this period, information on pain, complications, hospital stays, readmissions, and quality of life will be collected. The study aims to provide important information about the safe introduction and use of the Hugo™ system for this established weight-loss procedure.
interventions: Sleeve Gastrectomy using Hugo RAS platform
primary_outcomes: Proportion of robotic sleeve gastrectomy procedures successfully completed using the Hugo™ Robotic-Assisted Surgery (RAS) system including LigaSure™ RAS without intraoperative conversion to conventional laparoscopy or open surgery.
title: HUGO-SLEEVE: Evaluating the Feasibility of Robotic Sleeve Gastrectomy With a New Platform

brief_summary:
Critically ill patients who require a breathing machine are routinely assessed with a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) to determine if they can safely breathe on their own. If the trial fails, the breathing machine must be continued. One common cause is weaning-induced pulmonary oedema (WIPO), in which the heart cannot handle the increased workload during spontaneous breathing, causing fluid to accumulate in the lungs. Although several markers can suggest WIPO, it is often diagnosed after the SBT has already failed. Earlier recognition could allow clinicians to treat the condition promptly, improving the success rate of subsequent trials.

This study will examine whether electrical impedance tomography (EIT)-a bedside monitor that tracks how air moves in the lungs-can help identify WIPO earlier. We will focus on how lung aeration changes in the first minutes of the trial and whether combining EIT with standard clinical measurements improves early prediction of SBT outcome and identification of WIPO.

Study procedures will take place during routine SBTs and are mostly non-invasive. Participants will undergo EIT monitoring, heart and lung ultrasound, ventilator measurements, and blood tests. Clinical care remains entirely according to the ICU team. Participants will be followed for up to 28 days.
title: Detecting Early Weaning-induced Pulmonary Oedema Using Lung Impedance Negative Trend During SBT

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, biological activity, and initial efficacy of PM647a, an investigational Prime Editing therapy, in adults and adolescents with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD).

AATD is caused by a mutation (change) in a gene called SERPINA1 that prevents the cells in your liver from producing a functional protein (alpha-1 anti-trypsin; AAT) that helps protect your lung tissue. PM647a is designed to precisely correct the prevalent disease-causing mutation (SERPINA1 Pi\*Z (E342K)) with the goal of restoring functional AAT. This is the first study of PM647a in humans. Participants will receive a single intravenous (IV) infusion of PM647a and will be monitored closely to evaluate safety, how the body responds to treatment, changes in AAT protein levels, and whether treatment may improve signs and symptoms of AATD.
primary_outcomes: Safety and tolerability of PM647a. Quantified by frequency and severity of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
title: A Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Prime Editing (PM647a) in Participants With Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency

brief_summary:
In the treatment of spinal cord injury (SCI) patients in the hyperacute setting, it is imperative to closely control mean arterial pressure (MAP) to ensure adequate spinal cord perfusion in the absence of properly functioning autonomic innervation. Standards of care in literature have historically been to maintain a mean arterial pressure of 85-90 mmHg for 5-7 days after injury. Currently in the ICU setting, this is typically performed using intravenous vasopressors like norepinephrine. Although effective, vasopressors carry risks including arrhythmias, peripheral ischemia, and prolonged ICU management.

Transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) has emerged as an alternative method for blood pressure augmentation in SCI patients, recently completing a clinical trial in chronic SCI patients with incredibly promising results. tSCS has yet to be trialed in the ICU setting, but it is expected that patient response should be similar to the chronic setting. This prospective feasibility study will evaluate whether tSCS can acutely increase MAP in adults with acute traumatic SCI admitted to the ICU. During a single study session, participants will receive transcutaneous stimulation while standard vasopressor therapy is maintained at a constant dose. A neurocritical care physician will be present throughout testing to ensure patient safety and standard clinical management.

The primary objective is to determine the feasibility and acute hemodynamic effects of tSCS in this population. Primary outcome measures include change in MAP from baseline and time to hemodynamic response following stimulation. Secondary outcomes include changes in heart rate, stimulation tolerability, adverse events, and participant-reported comfort and overall experience. Data collected from this feasibility study will be used to assess the safety and practicality of implementing tSCS in the hyperacute SCI setting and to inform the design of future clinical trials evaluating tSCS as an adjunct or alternative strategy for blood pressure augmentation in critically ill SCI patients.
primary_outcomes: Time required to achieve peak MAP response
title: Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation for Blood Pressure Augmentation Immediately After Spinal Cord Injury

brief_summary:
The purpose of this observational study is to learn about the effects of the study medicine (called abrocitinib) for the treatment of severe atopic dermatitis in people that were moved from previous novel therapies, known as "advanced" therapies.

Atopic dermatitis is a long-lasting skin condition that causes the skin to become inflamed, dry, and itchy.

This study is seeking participants who:

* are 18 years of age or older;
* have severe atopic dermatitis;
* have previously been treated with advanced therapies authorised for atopic dermatitis and are moving to abrocitinib (100 mg or 200 mg);
* have received no more than two authorised advanced therapies for their atopic dermatitis.

All participants will receive study medicine, abrocitinib as part of their usual medical care. The decision to give the study medicine is made by their dermatologist. This decision is independent of participation in the study. Abrocitinib will be taken by mouth at home once daily as prescribed by the treating doctor.

We will examine the experiences of people receiving abrocitinib for up to one year after starting abrocitinib. We will look back at the information up to 6 months before they have started taking abrocitinib. This will help us learn how abrocitinib affects severe atopic dermatitis in people who have moved from other authorised advanced therapies.

Participants will take part in this study for 1 year. During this time, they will have about 5 visits. These visits are a part of their routine care. During the visits, the doctor will assess how severe atopic dermatitis is. Participants may be asked questions about their symptoms and how the condition affects their daily life.

No additional clinic visits, tests, or procedures are required for this study, beyond normal clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) <7
title: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Abrocitinib in People With Severe Atopic Dermatitis Who Have Switched From Other Therapies

brief_summary: General fatigue is a multidimensional symptom involving physical, cognitive, emotional, and motivational aspects, and it is closely associated with reduced daily functioning and quality of life. In patients with heart failure, fatigue is particularly complex and may persist despite rest. The Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI) assesses five dimensions of fatigue and has demonstrated good reliability and validity in its Taiwan Traditional Chinese version (MFI-TC) among healthy adults. However, its psychometric properties and clinical usefulness in patients with heart failure have not yet been systematically evaluated.
title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Traditional Chinese Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory in Patients With Heart Failure

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if giving intravenous immunoglobulin directly to the fetus during intrauterine transfusion can improve newborn outcomes in pregnancies affected by rhesus isoimmunization.

Rhesus isoimmunization happens when a pregnant woman's immune system attacks her baby's red blood cells. This can cause severe anemia (low red blood cell levels) before birth. Doctors treat this condition with intrauterine transfusion, a procedure that gives blood to the fetus before birth. However, this treatment does not stop the immune attack. Many newborns still develop anemia and high bilirubin levels after birth and may need phototherapy or exchange transfusion.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does adding fetal intravenous immunoglobulin increase the baby's blood count at birth? Does it lower the need for phototherapy or exchange transfusion after birth?

Researchers will compare:

Intrauterine transfusion with fetal intravenous immunoglobulin to Intrauterine transfusion alone to see if adding immunoglobulin improves newborn outcomes.

Participants will:

* Undergo intrauterine transfusion as part of routine care
* Be randomly assigned to receive either standard transfusion alone or transfusion with added fetal immunoglobulin
* Be followed until delivery and during the newborn hospital stay

The main outcome is the baby's blood count at birth. Researchers will also measure:

* How quickly the baby's blood count falls before birth
* Need for and duration of phototherapy
* Need for exchange transfusion or blood transfusions after birth
* Any procedure-related complications

This study will help determine whether treating the immune process before birth can improve health outcomes for newborns affected by rhesus isoimmunization.
conditions: Erythroblastosis Fetalis Due to RH Antibodies
lead_sponsor: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh
title: Neonatal Outcomes on Direct Fetal Intravenous Immunoglobulin During Intrauterine Transfusion for Rhesus Isoimmunization

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to compare postoperative pain after root canal treatment using two different types of ProTaper file systems: manual (hand-held) and rotary (engine-driven). A total of 186 participants aged 18-60 years with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis (with or without symptomatic apical periodontitis) requiring primary root canal treatment on a single tooth will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A will receive root canal instrumentation using ProTaper Manual files, and Group B will receive instrumentation using ProTaper Rotary files. Both groups will undergo a standardized single-visit root canal treatment protocol. Postoperative pain will be assessed using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at 6 hours, 12 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, and 72 hours, and 7 days after treatment. The study hypothesis is that there is no statistically significant difference in postoperative pain between the two instrumentation techniques. The findings will help clinicians choose the most appropriate instrumentation technique to minimize patient discomfort and improve treatment satisfaction
lead_sponsor: College of Physicians and Surgeons Pakistan
title: Comparison of Postoperative Pain After Root Canal Treatment Using Hand-Held vs Rotary ProTaper Files: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a bundle of three treatments can prevent atrial fibrillation, a heart rhythm disorder often observed in adults following heart surgery. Atrial fibrillation is associated with increased risks of stroke and heart failure. The bundle consists of two drugs (colchicine and amiodarone) as well as a simple surgical technique called posterior pericardiotomy. The main question it aims to answer is whether this bundle can reduce the incidence of atrial fibrillation after heart surgery.

Researchers will compare the results from this bundle of treatment to two other groups, one treated only with the posterior pericardiotomy and one treated following standard of care.

Participants, depending on their group, may receive colchicine and amiodarone before and just after heart surgery and the posterior pericardiotomy will be performed at the same time as the heart surgery.
primary_outcomes: Difference in the number of patients presenting an episode of persistent AF between control group and the two experimental groups
title: Randomized Interventional Clinical Trial on the Prevention of Atrial Fibrillation Using Colchicine, Amiodarone And a Posterior Pericardiotomy.

brief_summary:
Moral distress may arise when health care professionals are unable to act in accordance with their professional values or believe that they have participated in, witnessed, or been unable to prevent situations that conflict with those values. Repeated or particularly difficult experiences may affect emotional well-being, professional identity, and the meaning associated with clinical work.

This single-group pilot study will evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects of Coping and Adaptation for Recovery from Moral Injury (CARE-MI), a four-session group intervention for clinical psychology residents in Spain. Each 90-minute session addresses one of four components: moral awareness, emotional flexibility, moral repair, and professional flourishing. The program is designed to help participants recognize morally difficult experiences, respond more flexibly to associated thoughts and emotions, review responsibility in a fair and contextualized way, and protect the values and resources needed for professional practice.

Participants will complete assessments before and after the intervention. Changes in moral distress and psychological well-being will be examined, together with indicators of intervention feasibility and acceptability.
primary_outcomes: Change in Moral Injury Assessed With the Health Care Moral Injury Scale
title: Coping and Adaptation for Recovery From Moral Injury: A Group Intervention for Clinical Psychology Residents

brief_summary:
Background Inadequate oral health can further compromise general health, particularly in elderly patients who are more susceptible to tooth loss, periodontal disease, and oral infections. These conditions can impair nutrition and overall well-being and are associated with increased risks of systemic diseases, underscoring the critical need for effective oral care in this population. Essential oils and various plant extracts have attracted considerable attention as potential natural medicinal products due to their proven antibacterial, antifungal, antiviral, and antioxidant properties. However, the precise effects and underlying mechanisms through which essential oil mouthwashes promote oral health remain incompletely understood.

Objective This study aims to evaluate the potential of a mouthwash formulated with a blend of tea tree, lemon, and bay laurel essential oils, which have long been recognized for their medicinal properties in alleviating inflammatory signs of intraoral mucosa and promoting both oral and gingival health, in comparison with/ without alcohol-based mouthwashes.

Methods

One hundred five community-dwelling elderly individuals were randomly assigned to one of three groups and used a designated mouthwash for oral care over 21 days. The study groups were as follows:

1. Essential oils mouthwash (tea tree, lemon, and bay laurel).
2. Chlorhexidine alcohol-free mouthwash.
3. Povidone-iodine alcohol-free mouthwash. Participants were instructed to use the assigned mouthwash for oral hygiene at least twice daily, in the morning and evening. Saliva samples were collected on day 1 (before using the mouthwash) and on day 21 to analyze oral microbiota and inflammation markers and assess oral health and the incidence of upper respiratory tract infections.

Expected Results The treatment group of community-dwelling elderly individuals using the essential oil mouthwash is expected to show a significant reduction in oral bacterial load, improvement in gingival inflammation and periodontal symptoms, and a decreased risk of upper respiratory infections compared to the control groups using alcohol-free mouthwashes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Oral Health Assessment Tool (OHAT) Score
Change in Halitosis Consequences Inventory (ICH) Score
title: Essential Oil Mouthwash - Oral Hygiene

brief_summary: This retrospective cross-sectional observational study aims to develop a customized, patient-specific CBCT-based method for assessing skeletal transverse discrepancies independent of dental compensation. A total of 120 previously acquired CBCT scans of patients aged 15-30 years will be evaluated and equally divided into skeletal Class I, Class II, and Class III groups (40 scans per group). The study will assess transverse skeletal and dental relationships using standardized CBCT measurements and will evaluate the intra- and inter-examiner reproducibility of the proposed methodology. The distribution and pattern of transverse discrepancies among the three skeletal classes will also be assessed.
lead_sponsor: October University for Modern Sciences and Arts
primary_outcomes: Customized Patient-Specific CBCT-Based Assessment of Skeletal Transverse Discrepancy
title: Customized CBCT-Based Assessment of Transverse Discrepancies

brief_summary: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) affects a substantial proportion of older adults undergoing major surgery and may alter pain processing, pain experience, and opioid use after surgery. This prospective observational cohort study will compare older adults with MCI and cognitively intact older adults undergoing major orthopedic and complex spine procedures. Participants will undergo preoperative assessment of cognitive function, quantitative sensory testing, heart rate variability, clinical pain, and biomarkers associated with Alzheimer's disease risk. Postoperative pain trajectories, opioid use, pain responsiveness, and cognitive outcomes will be evaluated for six months following surgery. The study aims to determine whether MCI is associated with differences in postoperative pain and opioid use outcomes and whether APOE4 status and plasma amyloid beta 42/40 ratio contribute to observed differences.
title: Postsurgical Pain and Opioid Use in Older Adults: Effects of Mild Cognitive Impairment

brief_summary:
Patients requiring surgical jejunostomy or gastrostomy often have advanced malignancy, multiple comorbidities, and limited physiological reserve, which may increase the risks associated with general anesthesia. Ultrasound-guided fascial plane blocks may provide an alternative anesthetic approach in selected high-risk patients.

This single-center retrospective observational study aims to evaluate anesthesia management and perioperative outcomes in adult patients who underwent open surgical jejunostomy or gastrostomy using fascial plane blocks as the primary anesthetic strategy between February 2024 and August 2026.

The primary outcome is successful completion of surgery without conversion to general anesthesia. Secondary outcomes include supplementary sedative and analgesic requirements, airway interventions, intraoperative adverse events, postoperative rescue analgesia, length of hospital stay, and in-hospital mortality.
primary_outcomes: Completion of Surgery Without Conversion to General Anesthesia
title: Anesthesia Management and Perioperative Outcomes in Awake Jejunostomy and Gastrostomy

brief_summary: Primary aldosteronism represents one of the leading causes of resistant hypertension. Circulating cholesterol is established as the exclusive substrate for adrenal aldosterone synthesis, and statins, which suppress cholesterol production, are currently widely applied in clinical settings. Emerging clinical evidence has demonstrated that in patients with essential hypertension, the plasma aldosterone level decreased by 43% (from 13.9 ng/dL to 7.9 ng/dL) after treatment with PCSK9 inhibitors. However, the effect of PCSK9 inhibitors with superior lipid-lowering efficacy combined with amlodipine besylate on aldosterone levels remains elusive. The present clinical trial adopted inclisiran, a PCSK9 inhibitor with well-documented clinical safety and robust lipid-lowering effects, in combination with amlodipine besylate. Through randomized grouping intervention and follow-up, this study aimed to compare the differential effects of two therapeutic regimens-inclisiran-based therapy and statin-based therapy-on plasma aldosterone levels, as well as improvements in a spectrum of clinical parameters including blood pressure , serum potassium and so on in patients with primary aldosteronism. The outcomes of this trial are expected to provide novel and more effective pharmacological strategies for the management of primary aldosteronism.
interventions: Lipophilic statins (such as Simvastatin, Atorvastatin, Fluvastatin, Lovastatin,Pitavastatin)
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in plasma aldosterone level
title: Comparing Inclisiran Versus Statin for Primary Aldosteronism

brief_summary: Chronic, noninfectious uveitis in children, associated with various systemic inflammatory diseases, carries a high risk of vision loss. Intestinal dysbiosis and the translocation of bacterial peptidoglycans (PG) that activate innate receptors recognizing PG could represent a common initiating mechanism, independent of the underlying disease. Studying these biological signatures in comparative cohorts could lead to a better understanding of the onset of uveitis and the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
title: The Microbiome in Uveitis and Pediatric Inflammatory Diseases

brief_summary: This study is a two-arm randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of an ecological momentary intervention (EMI) in reducing psychological distress among young adults with multiple adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). The intervention targets three potentially modifiable transdiagnostic psychological processes: emotional clarity, self-esteem, and catastrophizing. Approximately 100 young adults aged 18-29 years who have experienced at least two types of ACEs and report elevated psychological distress will be recruited. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the EMI intervention group or the waitlist control group. Those assigned to the intervention group will receive a 2-week smartphone-based EMI delivered in their daily lives. Intervention effectiveness will be evaluated by comparing changes in psychological distress and related psychological outcomes between the two groups.
title: EMI for Reducing Psychological Distress in Young Adults With Multiple ACEs: A RCT Study

brief_summary: This is a single-center, prospective, randomized crossover physiological trial conducted in elderly patients (≥65 years) with septic shock in the intensive care unit (ICU). All enrolled patients receive sequential titration of mean arterial pressure (MAP) to three predefined target ranges (60-65 mmHg, 65-70 mmHg, and 70-75 mmHg) in randomized order. The primary objective is to compare tissue perfusion pressure (TPP) between the low and intermediate MAP targets, and to test the non-inferiority hypothesis that the lower MAP target is non-inferior to the intermediate target. Multiple secondary microcirculatory, systemic perfusion, and safety indicators are collected during steady-state hemodynamic periods under each MAP target stage. Researchers will adopt linear mixed-effects models to analyze intra-individual differences across blood pressure targets and explore the MAP threshold for optimal peripheral perfusion. Safety outcomes including adverse hemodynamic events and long-term clinical follow-up data will also be assessed.
primary_outcomes: Mean difference in Tissue Perfusion Pressure (TPP) between MAP target 60-65 mmHg and 65-70 mmHg
title: Perfusion Efficiency-Guided MAP De-escalation in Elderly Septic Shock

brief_summary: This Single-blind, randomized controlled trial will evaluate the effects of 12 weeks of combined VR-guided diaphragmatic breathing (Flowborne) and VR-aerobic cycling (Kinneta) compared with conventional pulmonary rehabilitation in male and female patients aged 45-55 years with stable COPD (GOLD Stage II). Both groups will train three times weekly at 65-75% HRmax. Primary outcomes are diaphragmatic excursion and FEV₁, while secondary outcomes include FVC, FEV1/FVC ratio, 6MWT, Borg dyspnea score, smoking index, SpO₂, and CAT score. All outcomes will be assessed at the end of the 12-week intervention.
primary_outcomes: Forced Expiratory Volume in One Second (FEV₁)
title: EFFECT OF COMBINED VIRTUAL REALITY-GUIDED BREATHING AND AEROBIC TRAINING ON VENTILATORY FUNCTION IN PATIENTS WITH COPD

brief_summary:
This trial is a 12-month safety and feasibility study, enrolling up to six participants. These participants will serve as their own controls, structured in multiple parts that follow an initial short-term stereo electroencephalography (SEEG) mapping period.

During this trial we aim to demonstrate the safety of acute and chronic network-guided stimulation in Mild Cognitive Impairment by evaluating adverse effects, tolerability, and feasibility during both the short- term SEEG mapping phase and subsequent permanent DBS therapy.

In addition to safety measures, therapeutic results as follows are to be tested for: (1) Develop patient-specific stimulation parameters for the treatment of MCI, as well as develop and test memory state classifiers by enrolling six individuals to undergo intracranial mapping (SEEG). We will use targeted memory tasks to generate neural data needed for state distinctions, and conduct a systematic parameter search to identify and develop optimal settings for each patient. (2) Assess efficacy of open loop stimulation by delivering a fixed open loop protocol based on the parameters discovered earlier, while SEEG electrodes remain in place, and testing the efficacy of the trained classifier to detect favorable brain states. (3) Evaluate chronic DBS therapy by implanting a permanent system in participants who show an acute beneficial response to assess long term outcomes. (4) Assess therapeutic outcomes and refine protocols by measuring reductions in memory-related impairment.

The above findings will guide further refinement of the device and protocol.
conditions: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) Due to Alzheimer's Disease
lead_sponsor: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
title: Deep Brain Stimulation Guided by Brain Mapping to Treat Cognitive Impairment

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial will evaluate the efficacy of a probiotic food supplement containing Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PBS067, Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus LRH020, and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL050 in women with recurrent uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs).

Seventy healthy non-menopausal women aged 18 to 50 years with a history of recurrent uncomplicated acute cystitis will be randomized 1:1 to receive either the probiotic supplement or placebo. Participants will undergo a 28-day intensive treatment phase followed by a maintenance phase consisting of 7 treatment days per month for approximately 4 months and a 28-day treatment-free follow-up period.

The primary objective is to evaluate the effect of the probiotic supplement on time to first recurrence of symptomatic uncomplicated UTI over a 24-week observation period. Secondary objectives include assessment of cumulative recurrence incidence, antibiotic use, urinary symptom severity, quality of life, fecal persistence of the probiotic strains, and changes in gut microbiota composition.
primary_outcomes: Time to first recurrence of a symptomatic uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI).
title: Probiotic Supplement for Recurrent UTIs in Healthy Women (L. Plantarum, L. Rhamnosus, B. Lactis)

The findings from this research may help explore the potential role of mangoes in a healthy diet for people at risk of developing type 2 diabetes

brief_summary:
Background:

AI (artificial intelligence) tools are increasingly used to help clinicians interpret medical images such as X-rays, scans, skin photographs and eye images. In most cases the AI does not work alone: a clinician makes the final decision, using the AI as support. Before these tools are used in the NHS, they must be tested to show they are safe and helpful. They are usually tested in a "reader study", where several clinicians each interpret the same set of images, sometimes with the AI's help and sometimes without, so performance can be compared. These studies tend to focus on whether the diagnosis was correct. However, accuracy alone may not measure everything that matters. For example, what happens when the AI gets it wrong, whether clinicians rely on it too much or too little, or how the tool affects efficiency. At present there is no agreed standard for what these studies should measure, so important things are often missed and studies are hard to compare.

Aim:

The aim of this study is to find out, by talking to people with different perspectives, which outcomes are important when evaluating AI tools that help clinicians read medical images.

Objectives:

1. Explore which outcomes people think matter when judging whether an AI tools is safe and good enough to use
2. Understand the reasons behind their views
3. Explore how priorities differ between groups, such as patients and developers.

The output will be a list of important candidate outcomes, which will feed into a future project to agree a recommended set of outcomes for these studies (a "core outcome set").

Research value:

Without agreement on what to measure, studies of AI tools may overlook outcomes that matter, and their results are difficult to compare and combine. Hearing directly from the people affected, rather than relying only on what previous studies happened to measure, helps ensure the recommended set reflects people's priorities. This will lead to better-designed studies and AI tools that are safer and more useful in practice.

Outline of the research:

The investigators will interview 24-30 people who have a stake in how these tools are tested and used, including clinicians, researchers, developers, people involved in regulation, and patients and members of the public. Interviews will last 45-60 minutes and will take place using Microsoft Teams. The investigators will ask people what they think is important to measure and why, and then explore which of those things could realistically be measured in a reader study.

Risks/benefits:

This is a low-risk study, with no direct benefits to participants. The topics concern methodological matters rather than people's personal health, so personal distress is not anticipated. Taking part is voluntary: interviewees can skip any question or stop at any time. The wider benefit will be better testing of AI imaging tools in future.

Impact:

The interviews will inform the candidate list of outcomes for the future project and the investigators will publish and present the findings.
title: What Should we Measure? A Qualitative Interview Study on Outcomes for Evaluating AI-assisted Medical Image Interpretation.

brief_summary: This randomized clinical trial will test whether a multimodal anti-inflammatory program added to standard treatment improves the prognosis of patients with heart failure who have recently been hospitalized or visited the emergency department for worsening heart failure. The program combines two parts: a structured physical exercise plan and a Mediterranean diet plan, adapted to each patient. A total of 214 adults with heart failure and mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (LVEF 40% or higher), recent worsening of heart failure, and elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein) will take part. Patients with frailty or malnutrition are excluded from the study. Patients will be recruited from heart failure clinics of participating Spanish hospitals. After agreeing to participate, patients will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: one group will continue their usual heart failure treatment, and the other will follow the same treatment plus the exercise and nutrition program delivered remotely by trained professionals for 12 months. The main question is whether the multimodal program reduces the combined occurrence of cardiovascular death, repeated heart failure hospitalizations, worsening exercise capacity (6-minute walk test), or worsening quality of life (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire) at 12 months. The study will also check whether the program lowers blood inflammatory and heart failure biomarkers (NT-proBNP, CA125), improves heart function on echocardiography, and whether patients' adherence to the program affects the results. All participants will continue to receive standard heart failure care; no medication is being tested, and the intervention consists of lifestyle coaching delivered by telephone or video calls.
primary_outcomes: Hierarchical composite of cardiovascular death, recurrent heart failure hospitalizations, 6-minute walk test distance, and quality of life (KCCQ) at 12 months
title: Exercise, Mediterranean Diet and Inflammation in Heart Failure

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational diagnostic imaging study is to evaluate the value of RET-targeted PET/CT molecular imaging in diagnosing neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and in assessing disease activity, treatment response, and prognosis. The study population consists of men aged 45-80 years, including approximately 40 patients with suspected or confirmed NEPC (positive group) and approximately 10 patients with conventional prostatic adenocarcinoma (negative control group).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can RET-targeted PET/CT imaging accurately diagnose neuroendocrine prostate cancer, using pathology as the gold standard? Compared with PSMA PET/CT, multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and serum markers, does RET-targeted PET/CT provide better diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values)? Is the level of RET tracer uptake in lesions associated with disease progression and prognosis, and can it be used for early assessment of treatment response? Researchers will compare RET-PET/CT imaging results against pathology (the primary reference standard), PSMA PET/CT, conventional contrast-enhanced MRI, and serum markers to determine the diagnostic advantage of RET-targeted imaging.

Participants will:

Sign a written informed consent form; Undergo whole-body PET/CT (and if needed, PET/MRI) imaging with RET- and PSMA-targeted tracers (approximately 0.15 mCi/kg injected intravenously; if a repeat scan is needed due to disease changes, it will be performed at least 1 week apart); Have blood pressure, pulse, respiration, and temperature measured before and after imaging, and liver/kidney function tests and routine blood and urine tests performed one day before and after imaging; Undergo multiparametric MRI (mpMRI); Be followed up, with any clinical symptoms or signs of discomfort during and up to two weeks after imaging recorded in detail.
conditions: Prostate Adenocarcinoma With Focal Neuroendocrine Differentiation
lead_sponsor: Xiangya Hospital of Central South University
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of RET-targeted PET/CT for neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC)
title: RET-Targeted Molecular Imaging Probes in Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to examine the effects of a web-based escape room (EQUITY-ROOM) and a web-based branching scenario (EQUITY-PATH) simulation added to standardized video-based education on nursing students' gender perception, dating violence myths, and dating violence attitudes.The study is designed as a 3-arm pretest-posttest parallel randomized controlled trial. The study begins with a cross-sectional survey to compare differences among these groups in terms of allergy-related markers, stool characteristics, and feeding difficulties. brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a personalized version of Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT), called MY PCIT, can improve treatment fit, treatment participation, and outcomes for young children with behavior problems and their caregivers. The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* How does standard PCIT compare to MY PCIT in keeping families engaged in treatment and improving treatment outcomes?
* How does standard PCIT compare to MY PCIT in aligning treatment and families' beliefs and values?

Researchers will compare standard PCIT to MY PCIT to learn how the personalized approach can be delivered in community mental health settings, and whether it may improve treatment fit, reduce treatment dropout, and improve outcomes for children and their caregivers.

Participating families will:

* Receive standard PCIT or MY PCIT
* Complete four sets of online surveys: one before treatment, two during treatment, and one after treatment

The surveys will ask about the child's behavior and the family's beliefs, values, and treatment experiences. Researchers will also gather feedback from therapists to help improve how MY PCIT can be delivered and sustained in community mental health sites.
primary_outcomes: Fidelity to PCIT and Fidelity to MY PCIT

brief_summary:
Sepsis and bloodstream infection (BSI) are among the most serious complications in patients with cancer, in whom disease- and treatment-related immunosuppression markedly increases susceptibility to infection. Sepsis accounts for approximately 15% of ICU admissions in this population, and short-term mortality is consistently higher than in patients without cancer (Bianchi et al., 2024).

In haematological malignancy, sepsis affects roughly 12-27% of patients within a year of diagnosis, and although in-hospital mortality has fallen over two decades, it remained higher than in non-cancer patients (23.1% vs 14.4% in 2021) (MacPhail et al., 2024).
interventions: Identification of bacterial isolates causing blood stream infection and determination of their antibiotic sensitivity
primary_outcomes: Identification of bacterial isolates causing blood stream infection and determination of their antibiotic sensitivity
title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Genomic Profiling of Bacterial Isolates

brief_summary:
This study aimed to investigate the relationship between instrumented balance measurements and clinical balance assessments in individuals with Parkinson's disease and to evaluate changes in balance and functional mobility following a 12-week multimodal rehabilitation program.

Eighteen individuals with Parkinson's disease participated in this prospective, single-group study. All participants received a rehabilitation program that included balance exercises, aerobic exercise, and balance training using the Korebalance system. The program was conducted twice weekly for 12 weeks.

Balance was assessed using the Korebalance system and the Berg Balance Scale (BBS). Functional mobility was evaluated using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test. Assessments were performed before and after the rehabilitation program.

The study examined whether instrumented balance measurements were associated with clinical balance performance and whether balance and functional mobility changed following rehabilitation.
title: Multimodal Rehabilitation and Balance Assessment in Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary:
The overall aim of this study is to evaluate the feasibility, implementation, public health effectiveness, durability, acceptability and cost of delivering long-lasting spatial emanators at scale through United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) humanitarian supply chains and distribution systems in northern South Sudan.

Primary objective:

To determine whether distribution of Guardian™ long-lasting spatial emanators reduces all-age malaria infection prevalence at 6 months in intervention populations compared with contemporaneous control populations during Phase 1 of the study.

Secondary objectives:

* Estimate the effect of Guardian™ on indoor and outdoor mosquito biting rate, including female Anopheles landing rates.
* Evaluate the feasibility and fidelity of humanitarian delivery through UNHCR supply chains, including timeliness, household coverage, adequacy of units relative to shelter volume, unpacking, correct placement and retention.
* Assess acceptability and safety, including user understanding, perceived benefit, barriers to use, product-related concerns and willingness to continue use or receive replacement units.
* Assess product durability and performance through field observations of physical integrity and quantitative chemical analysis of retrieved units.
* Describe changes in routine health facility malaria indicators and household-reported febrile illness as complementary measures of public health impact.

Tertiary and exploratory objectives:

* Estimate the cost and cost-efficiency of humanitarian delivery, including cost per unit delivered, household reached, person protected and correctly protected person-month, and estimate cost-effectiveness where supported by effectiveness data.
* Examine whether coverage, dose adequacy, correct placement, retention, shelter characteristics, population movement, seasonality and other contextual factors explain heterogeneity in epidemiological or entomological effects.
* Compare implementation performance and acceptability across different beneficiary groups (refugee camps, host communities and newly arriving displaced populations).
* Integrate epidemiological, entomological, implementation, qualitative, durability and economic findings to inform transition of long-lasting spatial emanators toward routine use as a humanitarian vector control commodity and guide future UNHCR, Ministry of Health and WHO implementation and scale-up decisions.
primary_outcomes: All-age malaria infection prevalence at 6 months following Phase 1 Guardian™ deployment
title: Humanitarian Evaluation of Spatial Emanators for Malaria Control

brief_summary: The purpose for this research project is to successfully achieve the primary systems intervention outcome, maintaining fidelity to the intervention model and time to rehospitalization. In the proposed research, the plan is to build the research infrastructure to ultimately test the effectiveness of CBIT on time to rehospitalization in a sample of rural Americans with SMI and determine the effective implementation strategies to bring the program to scale to address the significant unmet needs of this population. The proposed research will improve scientific knowledge and clinical and community practice by identifying the CBIT intervention's key components associated with enhancements in overall wellness and the mechanisms through which these improvements are attained. This may also better inform the practical and logistical design of future research for CBIT.
title: Community-Based Intensive Treatment (CBIT): Meeting the Complex Needs of Rural Adults With Serious Mental Illness

brief_summary:
A parapneumonic pleural infection is a frequently encountered and serious medical emergency with high morbidity and mortality in specific patient groups (especially in the elderly and immunocompromised). The burden of disease is high; extensive hospital stays, reduced Health-Related Quality of Life (HR-QoL) and long times to return to daily activities or to work are reported by patients and in studies. Standard care of pleural infections consists of placement of a chest tube and antibiotics. It is estimated that approximately 50% of patients with a pleural infection can be treated successfully with this strategy. When standard care fails, two main treatment modalities are available. One is intrapleural enzymatic therapy (IET), where medication is inserted through the chest tube. The other modality is minimally invasive surgery by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Although both modalities are extensively used, no consensus exits on which modality is superior or more cost-effective. This has led to extensive practice variation throughout hospitals in the Netherlands and to prolonged treatment episodes. The scarce literature on the subject to date appears to favor VATS in terms of treatment duration, but this is not supported by solid scientific evidence.

The primary objective is to provide decisive evidence on which treatment modality is superior for the treatment of pleural infections. This evidence will help to guide future treatment decisions and will lead to optimal and cost effective treatment of pleural infections. In order to provide this evidence, the investigators aim to investigate which modality results in the shortest length of hospital stay (LOS). In addition, the investigators want to investigate which modality is superior in terms of patient-reported outcomes (PROMs), complications, re-interventions and mortality.

The main trial endpoint is LOS during the first 30 days. This is defined as the time from the moment of chest tube insertion to the date of discharge.
title: VATS or Intrapleural Enzymatic Therapy for Patients With Empyema.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding functional electrical stimulation (FES) to a shoulder exercise program improves how the shoulder muscles work together in older adults with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain. FES uses small electrical currents delivered through pads on the skin to help muscles contract.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does exercise combined with FES improve coordination between the rotator cuff and deltoid muscles more than exercise alone?
2. Does exercise combined with FES increase the space between the top of the upper arm bone and the shoulder blade (acromiohumeral distance), which may reduce pinching of the shoulder tendons?

Researchers will compare a group that receives resistance exercise with FES to a group that receives the same resistance exercise without FES.

Participants will:

1. Attend exercise sessions 3 times per week for 4 weeks (12 sessions)
2. Complete 4 testing visits: before training, after 2 weeks, after 4 weeks, and 4 weeks after training ends
3. At each testing visit, perform shoulder strength tasks while muscle activity is recorded with sensors on the skin and thin wire sensors placed in the muscle, have an ultrasound of the shoulder, and complete questionnaires about shoulder pain and function
primary_outcomes: Intermuscular EMG Coherence During Submaximal Isometric Contractions
Intermuscular EMG Coherence During a Fatiguing Contraction
title: Functional Electrical Stimulation Combined With Exercise for Rotator Cuff-Related Shoulder Pain in Older Adults

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, observational, multicenter real-world study designed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of photodynamic therapy (PDT) in women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2).

Approximately 1,000 women aged 18 to 50 years with biopsy-confirmed CIN2 and a positive human papillomavirus (HPV) test will be enrolled. Participants will receive PDT that is approved for the treatment of CIN2 in routine clinical practice. Treatment will be administered according to the approved product labeling and the treating physician's clinical judgment. As this is an observational real-world study, the number and timing of PDT treatments will not be prespecified and will be recorded according to routine clinical practice.

Participants will be followed for 12 months after the initial PDT treatment. The primary outcome is the pathological remission rate at 6 months after the initial PDT treatment. Pathological remission is defined as a cervical biopsy showing normal tissue or CIN1/low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL).

Secondary outcomes include HPV clearance rates at 3 and 6 months, the incidence and severity of treatment-related adverse events, and the pathological remission rate at 12 months. Exploratory analyses will evaluate the association between available HPV-related biomarkers, including HPV integration status, and treatment outcomes.
title: RWS of PDT for CIN 2

brief_summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is among the most common malignancies in China, and approximately half of all patients develop liver metastases. For patients with resectable or potentially resectable liver-only metastases, R0 metastasectomy followed by perioperative chemotherapy is the current standard. However, recurrence rates remain high, especially in patients with high recurrence risk. This phase III study investigates whether an additional 6 months of adjuvant extended therapy with the oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor fruquintinib combined with capecitabine improves disease-free survival compared with guideline-recommended observation, in patients who have completed R0 resection and at least 3 months of perioperative chemotherapy for liver-only metastatic CRC.

brief_summary:
Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common condition caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist. It may cause pain, numbness, tingling, reduced hand function, decreased grip strength, and impaired quality of life.

This randomized controlled trial compared the effects of a technology-assisted multimodal rehabilitation program with conventional physiotherapy in adults with mild-to-moderate carpal tunnel syndrome.

A total of 40 participants were randomly allocated to two groups. The technology-assisted rehabilitation group used the ErgoActive system with Leap Motion sensor technology, while the conventional physiotherapy group received conventional physiotherapy. Both groups received 18 treatment sessions over six weeks.

The primary outcome was symptom severity, assessed using the Symptom Severity Scale of the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ-SSS). Secondary outcomes included pain intensity, functional status, hand-related quality of life, and grip strength. Pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS), functional status using the Functional Status Scale of the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ-FSS), hand-related quality of life using the Michigan Hand Outcomes Questionnaire (MHQ), and grip strength using a grip strength measurement device.

All outcomes were assessed before and after the treatment period. The study aimed to determine whether technology-assisted multimodal rehabilitation provides greater improvements in symptoms, pain, hand function, grip strength, and hand-related quality of life than conventional physiotherapy.
primary_outcomes: Symptom Severity Assessed Using the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ-SSS)
title: Effects of Technology-Assisted Rehabilitation on Pain and Hand Function in People With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding case-manager support to app-connected home blood pressure monitoring improves blood pressure control in adults with hypertension.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does case-manager surveillance with physician-guided medication adjustment lower office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure more than home monitoring with review of readings only at clinic visits?
* Does it change how consistently participants measure their blood pressure at home, how their blood pressure medicines are adjusted, and how often side effects are reported?

All participants received the same Bluetooth upper-arm blood pressure monitor linked to a smartphone app (OMRON Home BP Monitoring System, HMS). They measured their blood pressure at home in the first week of every month, following the Taiwan "722" schedule: 7 consecutive days, morning and evening, 2 readings each time.

Each participant spent 6 months in each of two conditions, in a randomly assigned order:

* Case-manager period: case managers reviewed the home readings every month, contacted participants, and arranged earlier clinic visits for medication adjustment when readings met predefined criteria.
* Control period: home readings were stored and reviewed by the cardiologist only at scheduled clinic visits.

Participants attended clinic visits at the start of the study and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months.
interventions: Case-manager surveillance with physician-guided remote titration
Passive data review at clinic visits
lead_sponsor: National Taiwan University Hospital Hsin-Chu Branch
title: Effect of Home and Remote Blood Pressure Monitoring Via Home BP Monitoring System (HMS) on Adults With Hypertension in Taiwan

brief_summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is an age-related movement disorder with a complex pathophysiology. Among the risk factors for PD, variants in beta-glucocerebrosidase (encoded by the gene GBA1) represent one of the most significant heritable risk factors for lifetime PD risk. Biallelic variants in GBA1 cause Gaucher disease (GD), a multisystem disorder, and individuals with late/adult-onset GD1 have a \~1-in-9 lifetime risk for PD. This study aims to develop a cross-sectional cohort of clinical and laboratory phenotyped adult GD1 patients and controls for investigation of clinical/laboratory risk factors for current and future Parkinson risk. Neurological evaluations will be video and audio recorded to allow the investigators to quantify neurological function using automated tools. Data and specimens generated in this study will be incorporated into a de-identified biobank that will be used for further research into GD and PD.

brief_summary:
Postoperative pneumonia (POP) affects 4%-24% of lung cancer surgery patients, increasing mortality, stay, costs and worsening prognosis, especially in older patients. Perioperative immunosuppression and synergistic influenza/pneumococcal infection support perioperative vaccination, which may also induce trained immunity; thoracic surgery data are lacking.

This multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint (PROBE) trial will enroll \~1278 patients aged ≥50 undergoing anatomical lung resection for pulmonary nodules or lung cancer, randomized 1:1 to vaccination or no vaccination, with 180-day follow-up.

Randomization uses a computer-generated, site-stratified block sequence, concealed via central IWRS or sealed envelopes. An unblinded team handles screening, randomization and vaccination data; surgeons and assessors are blinded. No site may exceed 50% of enrollment.

Vaccination group receives 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide and quadrivalent influenza vaccines intramuscularly in separate arms 14-28 days preoperatively. Controls receive no vaccine/placebo, with surgery scheduled 14-28 days after randomization. Concomitant indicated treatments are permitted and recorded.

Primary endpoint is POP per modified CDC/NHSN criteria: new/progressive imaging infiltrate (excluding atelectasis, edema, embolism, tumor), plus ≥1 clinical sign (fever \>38 °C, WBC ≤4000 or ≥12,000/mm³, or altered mental status if ≥70 years) and ≥2 respiratory signs. Findings on days 3-5 are excluded unless persistent/worsening. Microbiology is confirmatory, not required.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with postoperative pulmonary infection within 30 days after surgery
title: Preoperative Pneumococcal and Influenza Vaccination to Prevent Postoperative Pulmonary Infection in Patients Undergoing Lung Resection for Pulmonary Nodules or Lung Cancer
