brief_summary:
Patients' independence in Medical Care and Rehabilitation (SMR) settings is typically assessed using functional scales such as the Barthel Index. However, these tools give little consideration to digital skills, which have become essential in everyday life (communication, access to healthcare, information seeking, and administrative procedures).

The Digital Skills Score ("Score d'Habileté Numérique", TSHN-SMR) was developed to provide a simple and standardized assessment of a patient's ability to use a smartphone through several common tasks that simultaneously involve cognitive and motor functions.

This study aims to determine whether digital skills constitute a relevant and ecologically valid indicator of functional independence in rehabilitation patients. Ultimately, the TSHN-SMR could complement traditional assessment tools by providing a measure that more closely reflects activities actually performed in daily life within an increasingly digital environment.
interventions: TSHN-SMR (Test Standardisé d'Habileté Numérique sur Dispositif Dédié)
primary_outcomes: Change in TSHN-SMR Total Score Between Admission and Discharge
title: Impact of Functional Rehabilitation on Digital Independence: Validation of a Novel Smartphone Use Score as an Indicator of Discharge Readiness in Medical Care and Rehabilitation.

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of acupressure applied to the LI4 (Hegu) and Qiu points before Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL) in patients with kidney or proximal ureteral stones. The study compares intraprocedural pain scores and procedural tolerance between an acupressure group, a sham acupressure group, and a standard care control group.
primary_outcomes: Pain Severity Assessed by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
title: Acupressure as Complementary Analgesia in Shock Wave Lithotripsy

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to find out whether the medication dexmedetomidine can be a safe and effective additional treatment for cancer patients whose pain is not well controlled by standard pain medicines (such as opioids).

The study includes 30 palliative care patients who still have significant pain despite standard pain treatment. All participants will receive dexmedetomidine, and outcomes related to efficacy and safety will be systematically observed.
title: Dexmedetomidine for Refractory Pain in Palliative Cancer Patients

brief_summary: The current study is an observational, prospective study. It will be conducted in the emergency operative theatre, Alfayoum University, Alfayoum, Egypt. Identification of difficult mask ventilation among obese population is crucial specially in emergency settings with high risk of aspiration pneumonia or hypoxemia. No clinical predicrors were identified up till now. While the patient lies supine with the head in neutral position, Ultrasound guided (high frequency- depth adjusted at 3-4 cm) will be placed in the in submental region to measure the distance between skin to hyoid bone . Hyoid bone will be identified as a hyperechoic shadow below the mentum. Three measures will be taken and the average will be calculated. All candidates will sign informed consent pre-scanning and retain their right to withdraw at any time without compromising their medical care. Exclusion criteria will include elective operations, patient refual, previous neck surgery, prescence of surgical emphysema, emergency cesarean section and submental abcess.
primary_outcomes: Ability of SHD to predict DMV in obese population undergoing emergency operations
title: Prediction of Difficult Mask Ventilation in Obese Population Undergoing Emergency Surgery

brief_summary: The overall goal of this project was to develop and evaluate Counter Bias Training Simulation (CBTsim) Healthcare - an anti-bias training program that is specific for healthcare professionals. First, a culturally diverse team developed CBTsim Healthcare scenarios based on an extensive review of the literature on healthcare disparities. Then, a randomized control trial was conducted with 91 nurses to test the effectiveness of CBTsim Healthcare. Nurses received approximately 2 hours of baseline testing, then 51 nurses (treatment group) received approximately 3 hours of CBTsim Healthcare training and the other 40 nurses (control group) watched a 90-minute documentary on bias, information which is more typical of current standard practice. Then, all 91 nurses received approximately 2 hours of post-intervention testing. Baseline testing included a demographic questionnaire, a prejudiced belief assessment scale, and three written patient care scenarios in which decisions and communications to the patient were documented. Post-intervention testing included a survey to assess engagement with the training, the same prejudiced belief assessment scale, and three different patient care scenarios. Three months after the intervention participants were surveyed to gather qualitative feedback on beliefs about training effectiveness and how it had impacted patient care. Finally, Press Ganey scores from the hospital (patient satisfaction with nursing care) were analyzed for a 3-month period before the intervention and again after the intervention to try and determine whether the training had a measurable impact on patient care in the hospital.
title: Counter Bias Training Simulation Healthcare

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study assesses the prevalence of previously diagnosed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and associated risk factors among Saudi adults aged 18 years and older living in Taif City, Saudi Arabia. Surveys and available medical records provide information on respiratory symptoms, smoking, environmental and occupational exposures, and medical history. The COPD Assessment Test (CAT) measures symptom burden. The study examines factors associated with COPD and respiratory symptoms to support local prevention and early detection efforts.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Previously Diagnosed Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
title: COPD Prevalence and Risk Factors Among Saudi Adults Over 18 in Taif

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to validate computed inspiratory muscle pressure (cPmus) for monitoring inspiratory effort in adults receiving pressure-targeted assist/control ventilation (P-A/C) who retain spontaneous breathing. Participants initiate their own breaths, with assistance from the ventilator. Researchers will compare cPmus with reference inspiratory muscle pressure calculated using an esophageal balloon catheter, a thin pressure-measuring tube placed in the esophagus. The study will look at how closely the two methods are related and whether they give similar results.

Participants will undergo simultaneous monitoring with cPmus and an esophageal balloon catheter during assisted P-A/C ventilation. Researchers will adjust positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) across four levels. The inspiratory pressure setting will remain unchanged. Researchers will record measurements from both methods at each PEEP level.
title: Computed Inspiratory Muscle Pressure to Monitor Inspiratory Effort During Pressure-Targeted Assist/Control Ventilation

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind controlled clinical trial will evaluate whether adjunctive photobiomodulation improves recovery after nonsurgical root canal treatment in adults with teeth diagnosed with symptomatic apical periodontitis.

Participants will receive standard nonsurgical root canal treatment and will be randomized to adjunctive photobiomodulation using the Fotona LightWalker Nd:YAG laser or to an identical simulated laser procedure without laser energy delivery.

The study will evaluate mechanical allodynia using maximum occlusal force measurements comparing the treated tooth with the contralateral asymptomatic tooth. Postoperative pain will also be assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale after percussion testing.
primary_outcomes: Change in Mechanical Allodynia Measured by Maximum Occlusal Force Difference
Change in Mechanical Allodynia Measured by Maximum Occlusal Force Difference
Change in Mechanical Allodynia Measured by Maximum Occlusal Force Difference
title: Photobiomodulation After Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical trial is to examine the impact of a chatbot-supported intervention based on the Transtheoretical Model (TTM) on smoking behavior, self-efficacy, decisional balance, and the urge to smoke among university students. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the chatbot-based support intervention, grounded in the Transtheoretical Model (TTM), have an effect on smoking behavior?
* Does the chatbot-based support intervention, grounded in the Transtheoretical Model (TTM), have an effect on self-efficacy levels?
* Does the chatbot-based support intervention, grounded in the Transtheoretical Model (TTM), have an effect on decisional balance?
* Does the chatbot-based support intervention, grounded in the Transtheoretical Model (TTM), have an effect on the urge to smoke? The researchers will compare the experimental group with a group that received no intervention to determine whether the chatbot is effective in influencing smoking behavior.

Participants will:

* Complete the preliminary assessment questionnaire.
* If you are in the experimental group, access the Telegram chatbot via the provided link and exchange messages with the bot once a week for a total of 6 weeks (each session will take approximately 10 minutes). Additionally, read the informational messages sent twice a week and try to incorporate the suggestions into your daily life.
* Complete the follow-up questionnaires that will be sent after 6 weeks and again after 3 months.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Reporting Smoking Cessation at Week 6
Change in Stage of Change for Smoking Cessation from Baseline to Week 6
Proportion of Participants Reporting Smoking Cessation at 3 Months After the 6-Week Intervention
Change in Stage of Change for Smoking Cessation from Baseline to 3 Months After the 6-Week Intervention
title: THE EFFECT OF A TRANSTHEORETICAL MODEL-BASED CHATBOT SUPPORT INTERVENTION ON SMOKING BEHAVIOR IN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS

brief_summary:
Background: Postural deviations of the shoulders, pelvis and spine are common in preschool and school-aged children and may contribute to musculoskeletal imbalance and pain. Corrective exercise and organised sport have each been shown to benefit posture, but the effect of combining them in a single programme has not been examined.

Aim: To determine the effect of a nine-month corrective multisport (CMS) training programme on upper-body posture in healthy preschool and school-aged children.

Methods: In a single-centre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial, 398 healthy children were randomised (1:1, block randomisation stratified by sex) to a CMS group or a control group (CON). The CMS group completed two 60-minute sessions per week for nine months, combining corrective strength and stretching exercises with multisport activities (soccer, basketball, handball, tennis). The CON group continued regular physical education. Upper-body posture was assessed before and after the intervention with the Contemplas 3D photogrammetric system (Templo software) by assessors blinded to group allocation.
title: Corrective Multisport Training

brief_summary: This study evaluated an integrated active-learning approach for teaching cell physiology to international medical students at Tehran University of Medical Sciences. The approach combined a modified Re-teaching, Guidance, and Enrichment (RGE) strategy with flipped classroom activities, peer-assisted small-group learning, and scenario-based learning. Students participated in four instructional sessions and completed a questionnaire about their learning experiences after the fourth session. The study aimed to evaluate students' experiences of the educational approach and identify its strengths, challenges, and potential areas for improvement.
primary_outcomes: Students' Perceptions of the Integrated Active-Learning Educational Intervention
title: RGE-Based Cell Physiology Education for International Medical Students

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to compare how often joint contractures in the arms and legs come back after two common types of reconstructive surgery: Z-plasty and full-thickness skin graft (FTSG).

A joint contracture is a tightening of scar tissue, most often after a deep burn, that limits how far a joint can move. Surgery can release the tight scar, but the contracture may return over time. Z-plasty rearranges nearby skin to lengthen the scar, while FTSG covers the released area with full-thickness skin taken from another part of the body. Previous studies have shown conflicting results about which technique has a lower risk of the contracture returning.

This study will review the medical records of patients who had contracture release surgery of the shoulder, elbow, wrist/hand, hip, knee, or ankle at Dr. Moewardi General Hospital, Surakarta, Indonesia, between 2016 and 2026. No new treatment or procedure will be given to patients, and all patient information will be kept anonymous.

The study hypothesis is that the rate of contracture recurrence differs between patients treated with Z-plasty and those treated with FTSG. The results may help surgeons choose the most suitable technique to reduce the risk of recurrence and improve patients' movement and quality of life.
title: Recurrence of Extremity Joint Contracture After Z-Plasty Versus Full-Thickness Skin Graft

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the acute effects of a circuit breathing intervention on nicotine withdrawal symptoms and respiratory parameters among youth who use e-cigarettes.
title: Circuit Breathing Exercise on Smoking Cessation Among Youth E-Cigarette Users

brief_summary:
Knee osteoarthritis is a common cause of chronic pain and difficulty with everyday activities, particularly in older adults. Some patients continue to experience clinically relevant knee pain despite medication, therapeutic exercise, physiotherapy, or other conservative treatments.

This prospective, multicenter study will evaluate changes in pain, physical function, health-related quality of life, and safety after low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) in adults aged 60 years or older with painful primary knee osteoarthritis. All participants will receive the same treatment, and there will be no control or sham-treatment group.

Participants will receive one course of low-dose radiotherapy to the study knee, consisting of six fractions of 0.5 Gy, for a total dose of 3.0 Gy, administered twice weekly on nonconsecutive days over approximately 3 weeks.

Clinical assessments will be performed before treatment and approximately 45 and 90 days after the last radiotherapy fraction. The main outcome is the change from baseline to Day 90 in average knee pain during the previous 7 days, measured on a 0-to-10 Numerical Rating Scale. The study hypothesis is that average knee pain will be lower at Day 90 than before treatment. Other outcomes include physical function, health-related quality of life, the participant's overall assessment of the affected knee, pain response, analgesic use, treatment completion, additional knee treatments, and adverse events.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Average Index-Knee Pain Intensity at Day 90
title: Low-Dose Radiotherapy for Painful Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary:
This international, multicenter, observational survey study aims to assess current clinical practices in preoperative airway assessment in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland at both the institutional and individual anesthesiologist levels.

The study focuses on the use of individual airway assessment parameters versus combined assessment scores, as well as current documentation practices. An initial survey will establish baseline practices before the anticipated publication of the updated German Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine (DGAI) guidelines in 2028. A follow-up survey will be conducted after guideline publication to evaluate potential changes in clinical practice.

The study aims to identify differences between the three participating countries and assess changes in airway assessment and documentation practices following the publication of the updated guidelines.
interventions: Structured Survey on Preoperative Airway Assessment
primary_outcomes: Use of Individual Airway Assessment Parameters Versus Combined Assessment Scores in Clinical Practice
title: Airway Survey - International Airway Assessment Practices (2023-2028)

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effect of combined supplementation with Channa striata extract and Curcuma domestica rhizome on nutritional status, inflammatory markers, and quality of life in patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis receiving standard anti tuberculosis treatment at public health centers in Medan City. Pulmonary tuberculosis is frequently accompanied by malnutrition, persistent systemic inflammation, and impaired quality of life, all of which can delay recovery and worsen clinical outcomes. Channa striata is a rich source of high quality protein and albumin that may support nutritional recovery, while Curcuma domestica contains curcumin with well documented anti inflammatory properties. This study will assess whether the combined supplementation provides additional benefits in improving nutritional status, reducing inflammatory markers, and enhancing health related quality of life compared with standard treatment alone. The findings are expected to provide evidence for a safe, affordable, and locally available nutritional intervention that may complement conventional tuberculosis management.
primary_outcomes: Health-Related Quality of Life Measured Using the EuroQol Five-Dimension Five-Level Questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L) Index
title: Channa Striata and Curcuma Domestica Supplementation in Patients With Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis

brief_summary: This study aims to learn how to best promote safe firearm storage in the community. Firearm injuries are a major public health concern, and securely storing firearms can help prevent accidental injuries, suicide, and unauthorized access. This research will test whether providing people with a choice of firearm storage devices improves safe storage practices compared to providing standard cable locks alone. Adults who are patients, visitors, or employees at participating Penn Medicine community health centers may choose to enroll by scanning a QR code displayed at the site. After reviewing study information and providing consent, participants will complete a short online survey about firearm ownership and storage practices. Participants will then be randomly assigned to receive either cable locks or a choice of storage devices such as a lock box and/or cable locks, which will be mailed to their home at no cost. Participants will receive firearm safety educational materials and will be asked to complete brief follow-up surveys by text message about one month and three months later. Some participants and health center staff may also be invited to participate in interviews about their experiences with the program. The goal of this research is to identify practical and acceptable ways for health systems to support safe firearm storage and reduce firearm-related injuries in diverse communities.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Reporting All Firearms Stored Securely at 30 Days
title: Firearm Secure Storage Device Distribution RCT

brief_summary:
Aim: This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of finger-painting intervention administered during nebulization therapy on the fear and anxiety levels of children.

Methods: This randomized controlled trial was conducted in the pediatric ward of a city hospital between August 2025 and February 2026. The study was completed with 106 children aged 3-6 years (study group = 53, control group = 53). The data were collected by using Demographic Information Form, Children's Fear Scale, and Children's Anxiety Scale-State Anxiety. The study group received finger-painting intervention during nebulization therapy, while the control group received only routine care.
title: The Effects of Finger Painting as an Intervention During Nebulization Therapy on Fear and Anxiety Levels in Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center, consecutive observational study evaluates clinical, metabolic, and endocrine factors influencing survival and clinical outcomes in adult patients undergoing temporary mechanical circulatory support at the Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit of Gottsegen Gyorgy National Cardiovascular Institute.

While traditional cardiovascular risk factors in critically ill patients are well established, non-cardiovascular variables such as endocrine dysfunction, previous functional and nutritional status, metabolic parameters and clinical complications significantly impact short- and long-term outcomes.

The study consecutively enrolls all eligible adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or Impella treatment. The primary objective is to evaluate 28-day and ICU mortality, while secondary objectives include characterizing cardiac and non-cardiac complications, nutritional status changes, and hormonal dysregulations.
title: Factors Influencing Outcomes in ECMO and Impella Patients: Metabolic and Thyroid Hormone Dynamics

brief_summary: The aim of this study was to reduce the aggression levels of preschool children and to improve their social emotional well-being and psychological resilience through a structured therapeutic play program. The study was conducted as a randomised experimental research with pretest-posttest control group. The total sample consisted of 68 children, 34 in the intervention group and 34 in the control group. Data were collected with an information form, the Aggression Orientation Scale for Children and the Social Emotional Well-Being and Psychological Resilience Scale for Preschool Children. The intervention group participated in seven structured therapeutic play program group sessions.
interventions: Structured Play Activity in Preschool Children
primary_outcomes: Change in Aggression Tendency Scale for 36-72-Month-Old Children Total Score
Change in Social Emotional Well-Being and Psychological Resilience Scale for Preschool Children (PERIK) Total Score
title: The Effect of Structured Therapeutic Play Program on Aggression, Social Emotional Well-Being and Psychological Resilience in Preschool Children

brief_summary:
Shoulder pain is a common musculoskeletal condition that can cause pain, movement limitations, disability, and difficulties performing daily and occupational activities. Rotator cuff-related shoulder pain (RCRSP) is one of the most common clinical presentations among people seeking care for shoulder problems.

Exercise therapy is recommended as a first-line conservative treatment for RCRSP. Progressive resistance training and motor control exercises can improve pain and shoulder function, while exercises targeting thoracic mobility and scapular and glenohumeral function may be useful for addressing individual movement and functional limitations. However, there is still uncertainty about the optimal selection, intensity, volume, and progression of exercises for individual patients.

Objective To analyze the effects of a shoulder school program led by a physiotherapist and based on therapeutic exercise focused on active scapular and thoracic work, compared to conventional treatment in patients with RCRSP referred to Primary Care Physiotherapy Units in Albania, regarding pain, functional capacity, and quality of life.

Methods Design: Single-blind, multicenter, prospective, randomized, controlled non-inferiority study.

Sample: Patients with RCRSP referred to primary care in Albania. Dependent Variables: Pain, functional capacity, quality of life, joint mobility, isometrical strenght, and patient satisfaction.

Independent Variables:

Intervention group: Shoulder school program including exercises focused on scapular, thoracic, and rotator cuff function.

Control group: Conventional physiotherapy treatment.

Randomization: Cluster randomization by centers. Analysis: Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 25.0.

Clinical Implications This study will provide objective data on the effects of implementing a group exercise program guided by a physiotherapist. The results could offer evidence for a resource that may be highly useful in Primary Care Physiotherapy. This approach has the potential to optimize labor, time, and space resources within this healthcare service.
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity measured with visual analogue scale
title: Implementation of Shoulder School in Albania

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the safety and preliminary effectiveness of sonrotoclax combined with azacitidine in adults aged 18-70 years with newly diagnosed myelodysplastic neoplasms with increased blasts-2 (MDS-IB2).

Sonrotoclax blocks BCL-2, a protein that helps cancer cells survive. Combining sonrotoclax with azacitidine may improve disease control. This study aims to determine whether the combination can induce remission with an acceptable safety profile, facilitate allogeneic stem cell transplantation in suitable patients, and improve long-term clinical outcomes.

This multicenter, open-label study has two sequential parts. Phase Ib will evaluate different sonrotoclax doses and identify the recommended dose for phase II. Phase II will further assess remission rates and safety at the selected dose. All participants will receive sonrotoclax plus azacitidine; there is no randomized control group.

Participants will undergo regular blood tests, bone marrow examinations, and monitoring for side effects. Suitable participants may proceed to transplantation based on disease response and clinical condition. Those who are not proceeding to transplantation and continue to benefit may continue treatment according to the protocol. Follow-up will assess the duration of remission, disease progression, subsequent treatment, survival, and quality of life.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai General Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Maximum Tolerated Dose / Recommended Phase 2 Dose
title: Sonrotoclax Plus Azacitidine in Patients With MDS-IB2

brief_summary: This completed study compared early-life feeding with organic infant formula and organic complementary foods, conventional infant formula and conventional complementary foods, and breastfeeding with family-selected complementary foods. Infants were recruited in Chenzhou, Hunan, China, and followed through 8 months of age. The study examined physical growth, early development, gastrointestinal symptoms, stool characteristics, and gut microbiota. Measurements and questionnaires were collected at baseline and scheduled visits at 2, 4, 6, and 8 months of age. The aim was to assess whether organic feeding was associated with differences in infant health and gut microbiota compared with conventional feeding, with breastfeeding as a natural reference. Registration is being completed retrospectively after the study has finished.
interventions: Organic infant formula and organic complementary foods
Conventional infant formula and conventional complementary foods
title: The Impact of Early-life Organic Feeding on Infants' Health: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This study aims to compare plantar fascia thickness and pedobarometric parameters between individuals with sacroiliak joint dysfunction and healty individuals.A total of 52 adult volunteers aged 18 to 50 years were included in the study, with 26 pariticipants in the sacroiliac joint dysfunction group and 26 participants in the healty control group.Participants with sacroiliac joint dysfunction were identified based on clinical examination and sacroiliac joint pain provocation tests. Foot posture was evaluated using the Foot Posture Index-6 (FPI-6), and participants with neutral foot posture were included. Plantar fascia thickness of both feet was measured using ultrasound. Static foot pressure measurements were performed during standing with eyes open and closed, and dynamic foot pressure measurements were performed during walking using a pedobarometric system. The study compares plantar fascia thickness and pedobarometric parameters between the sacroiliak joint dysfunction and control groups. It also investigates the relationship between plantar fascia thickness and pedobarometric parameters.
title: Plantar Fascia Thickness and Pedobarometric Parameters in Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction

brief_summary: This Phase 1b/2, open-label, multicenter, single-arm study evaluates the safety and efficacy of ivonescimab in combination with pemetrexed and platinum-based chemotherapy as first-line treatment for advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma. Phase 1b evaluates the candidate recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D), followed by Phase 2 evaluation at the confirmed RP2D.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ivonescimab Plus Pemetrexed and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Advanced Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma

brief_summary: This study aimed to develop an educational program for the prevention of disordered eating behaviors among middle school students and to evaluate its effectiveness. The study was conducted with seventh-grade students and their parents at a middle school in Izmir, Türkiye. Classes were randomly assigned to the intervention and control groups. The three-week educational program focused on body image, social media literacy, and healthy eating attitudes. The effects of the program were evaluated by comparing eating attitudes, body satisfaction, social media literacy, sociocultural appearance attitudes, dietary quality, nutrient intake, and anthropometric measurements between the groups over time.
interventions: School-Based Disordered Eating Prevention Education Program
primary_outcomes: Change in Eating Attitudes Test-26 (EAT-26) Score
title: A School-Based Intervention to Prevent Disordered Eating in Middle School Students

brief_summary:
This is a Phase I, dose-escalation study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of Recombinant Anfibatide Injection in healthy adult volunteers.

Approximately 36 healthy participants will receive a single intravenous dose of either study drug or matching placebo across sequential dose cohorts. Safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic parameters will be assessed following administration.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and Severity of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)
title: Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Recombinant Anfibatide Injection in Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary: Effect of Preoperative Methotrexate on Intraoperative Blood Loss and Surgical Outcomes During Laparoscopic Management of Cesarean Scar Pregnancy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
title: Effect of Methotrexate on Blood Loss During Laparoscopic Management of CS Scar Pregnancy

brief_summary: This study uses clinical vignettes to explore how healthcare professionals make complex ethical decisions in intensive care settings. Participants evaluate several simulated scenarios, and their responses are analyzed to better understand decision making patterns.
primary_outcomes: Decision rating on a 4 point Likert scale
title: Implicit Bias in Intensive Care: Analysis and Assessment.

brief_summary:
As more older adults use the internet to seek health information, it may be difficult to determine whether online information is trustworthy. Social media posts, advertisements, messages, and product promotions may contain misleading information or scams. This study will examine whether a practical fact-checking course can help older adults make more accurate judgments about online health information.

Approximately 100 older adults from senior learning centers in northern Taiwan will participate in this study. Participants will be assigned to one of two groups. The experimental group will receive a four-week health information fact-checking course, and the control group will receive a four-week nutrition education course. Both groups will participate in learning activities; however, only the fact-checking course will involve digital tools and examples of online health information.

Participants in the fact-checking course will practice evaluating health information through common real-life situations, including health-related social media posts, online product advertisements, free-gift promotions, and suspicious text messages. The course will teach a fact-checking method called SIFT:

Stop: Pause before believing or sharing information. Investigate the source: Check who created or posted the information. Find better coverage: Look for other reliable sources that discuss the same claim.

Trace claims to the original context: Locate the original source and determine whether the claim has been presented accurately.

Before and after the four-week intervention, participants will complete questionnaires and short activities concerning the use of online health information and the evaluation of health-related messages. The investigators will compare outcomes between the two groups to determine whether the fact-checking course improves confidence and accuracy in judging online health information.

This study may inform the development of digital health learning programs for older adults.
lead_sponsor: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
title: The Effects of a Scenario-based Fact-checking Course on eHealth Literacy and Fact-checking Skills Among Older Adults.

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn how short exercise breaks, often called exercise snacks, on stationary exercise bikes can best be offered during the school day to students in Primary 4 to 6 at an inclusive primary school in Macao, including autistic students. It will also learn whether the program is practical and safe in an inclusive school.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

When the bike screen shows a game with points and a ranking among the four riders in the group, do students ride farther per scheduled minute than when the same screen shows a regular display with a cartoon cyclist, heart rate, distance and time remaining? Is any extra riding on game days larger when the 10 minutes are ridden at once than when they are split into two 5-minute rides, and is it accompanied by better or worse feelings during and after the ride? When the same 10 minutes are split into two 5-minute rides, do students receive the same riding dose and are they as focused on their classwork afterwards? How many planned rides actually happen and are completed, and what support do autistic students need?

The investigators expect students to ride more on game days. Whether that extra riding comes with better or worse feelings, and whether it depends on ride length. The comparison with the waitlist group only estimates how large the differences are, to help plan a larger study.

Thirty-two riders ride in fixed groups of four on 3 fixed school days a week for 8 weeks, 10 minutes a day: one 10-minute ride a day for 4 weeks and two 5-minute rides a day for the other 4 weeks. Within each 4-week period, the display shown to a group on each riding day is randomly assigned, with equal numbers of game and regular-display days, and the same virtual tracks are used under both displays. Riders wear a heart-rate arm band and answer a few picture-supported questions before, during and after each ride. Trained observers, who do not know which display or schedule students are on, record how focused students are on their classwork in the lesson after riding. Sixteen waitlist students follow the usual school routine, complete the same assessments, and receive access to the bikes after the study. All students complete a short tablet attention task and questionnaires about exercise motivation and quality of life before and after the 8 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Distance per scheduled minute (km/min) recorded by the stationary-bike software on each riding day
title: Gamified Versus Regular Exercise Snacks on Stationary Bikes, as One 10-Minute or Two 5-Minute Sessions a Day, for Children in an Inclusive Primary School

brief_summary: This single-centre randomised pilot study compared two strategies for primary abdominal access and gallbladder extraction in elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy: open (Hasson) umbilical access with extraction of the gallbladder through the umbilical incision, and closed (Veress needle) access with extraction through the epigastric port. Access time, gallbladder extraction time, total operative time and postoperative pain were compared. Enrolment was stopped in March 2020 when elective laparoscopic surgery was suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic. This trial was registered retrospectively
interventions: Hasson open access and umbilical gallbladder extraction
Veress needle access and epigastric gallbladder extraction
title: Hasson Versus Veress Access With Umbilical Versus Epigastric Gallbladder Extraction in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary:
This is a nationwide, multi-center, long-term follow-up study of overweight and obese adults in China. The study aims to recruit approximately 26,000 participants across 39 hospitals to better understand how body weight affects the development of obesity-related diseases over a 3-year period.

Eligible participants are adults aged 18 to 79 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m² or higher. Participants will be grouped into four categories based on their BMI: overweight, mild obesity, moderate obesity, and severe obesity.

At the beginning of the study, all participants will undergo a comprehensive health assessment, including physical measurements, body composition analysis, blood tests, and lifestyle questionnaires. Participants will then be followed for 3 years with annual check-ins to track any new health conditions.

The main goal is to identify the 3-year risk of developing conditions such as type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, high blood pressure, and heart disease in different weight groups. This information will help doctors better predict and prevent obesity-related health problems in the future.

Participation is voluntary, and all personal information will be kept confidential.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)
title: Chinese Overweight/Obesity Cohort: Metabolic & Comorbidity Risks

brief_summary:
Spinal anesthesia is the preferred technique for elective cesarean section, but it frequently causes maternal hypotension due to sympathetic blockade and the Bezold-Jarisch reflex, which can threaten both mother and baby. Ondansetron, a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist commonly used to prevent nausea and vomiting, may attenuate this reflex.

The purpose of this prospective, randomized, controlled, single-blind study is to evaluate whether a single prophylactic intravenous dose of ondansetron (4 mg) given before spinal anesthesia reduces the incidence of hypotension in women undergoing elective cesarean section. Vasopressor (ephedrine) requirement, heart rate, postspinal shivering, intraoperative nausea and vomiting, and newborn Apgar scores are also compared between the ondansetron and control (saline) groups.
lead_sponsor: Saglik Bilimleri Universitesi Gazi Yasargil Training and Research Hospital
title: Prophylactic Ondansetron for Preventing Spinal Anesthesia-Induced Hypotension in Elective Cesarean Section

brief_summary:
This study compares two different root canal sealers, AH Plus and BioRoot Flow, to determine whether the type of sealer used during root canal treatment affects pain after treatment and oral health-related quality of life.

Root canal treatment is performed to treat infection inside a tooth. Some patients may experience pain or discomfort after treatment, which can affect their daily activities and well-being.

The study includes adults with asymptomatic apical periodontitis in a permanent tooth with one root and one root canal. Participants are randomly assigned to receive root canal treatment using either AH Plus, a resin-based sealer, or BioRoot Flow, a bioceramic-based sealer. All participants receive treatment in a single visit.

Pain after treatment is assessed using a visual analog scale at 6 and 12 hours and on days 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, and 30. brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-dose, dose-escalation Phase Ib clinical study designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) characteristics, immunogenicity, and clinical efficacy of EB070 Injection in adult patients with moderate-to-severe asthma. The study will also explore the optimal dose for achieving biological effects and the recommended dose for Phase II development.

Based on the results of the Phase I study in healthy participants, two ascending dose groups are planned: 225 mg and 600 mg, administered sequentially across study centers. The doses are provisional and may be adjusted based on the results of the Phase I study in healthy participants and the emerging results of this study. Each dose group is planned to enroll 10 participants, who will be randomized in a 4:1 ratio to receive EB070 Injection or placebo by subcutaneous injection into the abdomen once every 4 weeks for a total of 4 doses. Approximately 20 adult patients with moderate-to-severe asthma are expected to be enrolled. Each participant may participate in only one dose group.

Dose escalation will proceed only after the Safety Review Committee (SRC), consisting of an independent unblinded third-party physician, the investigator, and the sponsor, confirms that all participants in the preceding dose group have demonstrated acceptable safety and tolerability within 2 weeks after the second dose. If predefined dose-escalation termination criteria are met, the SRC will review the safety data and may consider returning to an intermediate dose between the affected dose and the preceding dose to further explore the maximum tolerated dose. If the highest dose specified in the protocol is reached without meeting the dose termination criteria, the SRC will determine whether escalation to a higher dose is appropriate. If a participant discontinues for reasons unrelated to safety, the SRC will determine whether additional participants should be enrolled in the affected dose group.

If any serious adverse event (SAE) related to the investigational drug occurs, or if ≥2 participants in a dose group experience similar Grade 3 adverse events related to the investigational drug, enrollment into the relevant dose group will be suspended. The SRC will conduct a comprehensive assessment of the event, including its severity, relationship to the investigational drug, time to onset, clinical manifestations, reversibility, and other available safety data. Enrollment may resume only after the SRC confirms that the risk is controllable and approves continuation of the study.

Potentially eligible participants will undergo screening assessments within 21 days before the first dose to determine eligibility. Eligible participants will undergo baseline assessments within 1 day before dosing (Day -1). For assessments such as physical examination, complete blood count, urinalysis, and blood chemistry, results obtained within 7 days before dosing may be used as baseline values. Participants confirmed by the investigator to meet all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria will undergo baseline PK and PD sample collection within 1 hour before the first dose.

Participants will subsequently receive four subcutaneous doses of EB070 Injection or placebo at 4-week intervals. During the study, participants will attend scheduled visits for study drug administration and collection of PK, PD, and immunogenicity samples, as well as assessments of safety, tolerability, and clinical efficacy according to the protocol-defined schedule.
title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase Ib Study of Multiple Ascending Doses of EB070 Injection in Adults With Moderate-to-Severe Asthma

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to understand how sleep and brain activity change after epilepsy surgery in adults with drug-resistant epilepsy. Drug-resistant epilepsy means that seizures continue despite treatment with appropriate medications.

The study will investigate whether changes in sleep and brain activity are related to seizure control, sleep quality, and quality of life after surgery.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do sleep patterns and brain activity change after epilepsy surgery?
* How are changes in sleep and brain activity related to seizure control and quality of life?
* Do sleep patterns after surgery become more like those of healthy adults?
* How are changes in blood proteins related to sleep, brain activity, and seizure control? Researchers will follow 30 adults undergoing epilepsy surgery. Their sleep will be compared with that of 10 healthy adults of similar age and sex. Healthy participants will complete the study assessments once.

Participants undergoing epilepsy surgery will complete the assessments before surgery and approximately 2 and 6 months after surgery.

At each assessment, participants will:

* Wear a small device (actigraph) on their wrist for about 2 weeks to measure sleep and activity and keep a sleep diary.
* Spend 2 consecutive nights at a patient hotel while their sleep and brain activity are recorded using polysomnography (PSG), a test that measures sleep, breathing, and brain activity.
* Answer questionnaires about sleep quality, insomnia, mood, and quality of life.
* Provide blood samples for research. Researchers will also collect information about seizure frequency, medications, and medical history.

The sleep recordings will be used to study several aspects of sleep, including:

* Sleep architecture: how much time participants spend in different stages of sleep and how often their sleep is interrupted.
* Sleep spindles and slow oscillations: patterns of brain activity during sleep that are involved in how the brain processes and organizes information.
* Cyclic alternating pattern (CAP): a measure of brief changes in brain activity during sleep that can provide information about sleep stability.
* Epileptiform activity: abnormal electrical activity in the brain that may be associated with epilepsy and can occur during sleep.

Researchers will also analyze proteins in blood samples to explore whether biological changes are related to sleep and seizure outcomes.

Epilepsy surgery and other medical treatments will be decided by the participants' treating healthcare teams, independently of this study. The study will observe changes before and after surgery without assigning participants to a treatment.

brief_summary:
Sedation and analgesia are essential components of comprehensive care for intensive care unit (ICU) patients, particularly those receiving invasive mechanical ventilation, undergoing invasive procedures, or experiencing pain, anxiety, agitation, and patient-ventilator asynchrony. Appropriate sedation and analgesia can alleviate pain and discomfort, improve tolerance of mechanical ventilation and other life-support therapies, and help maintain treatment safety.

In recent years, the paradigm of ICU sedation has gradually shifted from traditional deep sedation toward management strategies centered on analgesia-first, light sedation, and individualized sedation targets. Clinical practice emphasizes regular assessment of pain, depth of sedation, and delirium, with dynamic adjustment of sedation and analgesia regimens according to the patient's condition. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) has been widely used to assess sedation depth in the ICU, while the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) is commonly used for delirium screening in critically ill patients.

However, in real-world clinical practice, sedation requirements vary considerably among patients, and the choice of sedative agents is still influenced by multiple factors, including patient age, underlying diseases, circulatory status, organ function, mechanical ventilation requirements, and physicians' prescribing habits. Currently commonly used sedatives include propofol, dexmedetomidine, and midazolam, as well as newer intravenous sedatives that have been gradually introduced into clinical practice in recent years, such as remimazolam and ciprofol. These agents may differ in sedative efficacy, hemodynamic stability, speed of emergence, delirium risk, and duration of mechanical ventilation; however, direct comparative evidence among them in real-world ICU patients remains limited.

Moreover, sedation management is not merely a matter of drug selection. Depth and duration of sedation, dose adjustment, rescue sedation, combination therapy, and analgesic exposure may all affect patients' neurological status and clinical outcomes. Excessive or prolonged sedation may lead to delayed emergence, prolonged mechanical ventilation, coma, and delirium, whereas inadequate sedation may increase the risks of agitation, patient-ventilator asynchrony, self-extubation, and unplanned device removal.

Therefore, it is necessary to establish a standardized, prospective clinical database for ICU sedation and analgesia that systematically records patient baseline characteristics, disease severity, use of sedative and analgesic agents, sedation depth, pain, delirium, organ support, and clinical outcomes, and to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of different sedation and analgesia strategies based on real-world clinical practice.

This study aims to establish a prospective, multicenter registry cohort of sedation and analgesia in critically ill patients. Without interfering with clinicians' therapeutic decisions, it will systematically evaluate the characteristics of ICU sedation and analgesia practice and their association with patient clinical outcomes, and provide a high-quality data foundation for subsequent comparative effectiveness research on different sedative agents and sedation strategies, target trial emulation (TTE), and individualized sedation strategy research.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of time within the target sedation range
Incidence of new-onset delirium at 7 days
title: A Prospective Multicenter Registry Study of Sedation and Analgesia in Critically Ill Patients

brief_summary: This phase II trial tests how well tacabrutideg and sonrotoclax, with response-guided addition of obinutuzumab, works in treating patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). Tacabrutideg is a drug that degrades a protein called Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). By degrading BTK, tacabrutideg inhibits the activation of signaling pathways that help cancer cells survive, inhibiting the growth of cancer cells that express the BTK protein. Sonrotoclax is in a class of medications called B-cell lymphoma-2 (BCL-2) inhibitors. It may stop the growth of cancer cells by blocking BCL-2, a protein needed for cancer cell survival. Obinutuzumab is a monoclonal antibody that may interfere with the ability of cancer cells to grow and spread. A monoclonal antibody is a type of protein that can bind to certain targets in the body, such as molecules that cause the body to make an immune response (antigens). Giving tacabrutideg together with sonrotoclax may kill more cancer cells than giving either drug alone, and giving obinutuzumab after initial treatment with tacabrutideg and sonrotoclax may improve disease response in patients whose CLL or SLL didn't respond completely to initial treatment.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants who have undetectable measurable residual disease at a sensitivity of 10^-4 (uMRD4)
title: Tacabrutideg and Sonrotoclax, With Response-Guided Obinutuzumab, for the Treatment of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)/Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (SLL)

When conventional treatments such as rehabilitation, physiotherapy, and activity modification do not provide sufficient improvement, surgical ligament repair may be recommended.

Although this surgery generally restores ankle stability, there is currently limited evidence regarding how lower-limb function evolves following the procedure. In particular, there is no established objective reference measure to assess functional recovery and support healthcare professionals in making decisions regarding rehabilitation or return to sport.

The prospective interventional comparative analysis proposed in this study aims to evaluate surgery-induced changes in ankle and lower-limb movement and function that can be objectively quantified through biomechanical motion analysis.

Constipation is a common and uncomfortable problem among patients receiving palliative care. Alongside usual treatment and nursing care, abdominal massage may help manage constipation. Teaching caregivers how to perform this massage may also help them feel more confident in supporting the patient.

This study aims to evaluate the effects of abdominal massage training for caregivers on patients' constipation, caregiver burden, and caregivers' confidence in contributing to patient self-care.

Patients and their primary caregivers will participate together. Both patients and caregivers must be aged 18 years or older. Patients must have constipation, have been hospitalized in a palliative care unit for at least two weeks, and have no clinical condition that prevents abdominal massage.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Caregivers in the intervention group will receive a single 45-minute training session that includes an explanation and a practical demonstration of abdominal massage. They will also receive a training booklet. After training, caregivers will perform abdominal massage for 15 minutes in the morning and 15 minutes in the evening, three days per week, for two weeks. Patients will continue receiving their usual treatment and care.

Patients and caregivers in the control group will continue with usual treatment and care during the study. Control-group caregivers will be offered abdominal massage training after their study participation is completed.

Patients' constipation severity and stool form, as well as caregivers' burden and confidence in contributing to patient self-care, will be assessed at the start of the study and on Days 7 and 14.

Ethical approval has been obtained from the University of Health Sciences Hamidiye Ethics Committee for Interventional Research Not Involving Drugs or Medical Devices. Institutional permission has been obtained from the study hospital before data collection. Written informed consent has been obtained from patients and caregivers. Participation is voluntary, and personal information will be kept confidential.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to develop and validate artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms that use subhairline EEG (a simplified EEG patch placed on the forehead and behind the ears) to predict neurological outcome and to detect intracranial hemorrhage. The study consists of two use cases: (UC1) adults (18 years or older) in postanoxic coma after cardiac arrest who are admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), and UC2) adults with suspected stroke or suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) who present to the emergency department. The primary objectives are:

* UC1: to develop and validate an AI-algorithm for outcome prediction in postanoxic coma at 24h after CA based on subhairline EEG.
* UC2: to develop and validate an AI-algorithm for detection of ICH among patients with (suspected) stroke based on subhairline EEG and clinical symptoms.

Participants will:

* UC1: receive a continuous subhairline EEG recording, in addition to the standard scalp EEG used in routine care. The recording starts as soon as possible after ICU admission and continues for up to 72 hours after cardiac arrest.
* UC2: receive a single subhairline EEG recording of about 2 minutes as soon as possible after arrival. Clinical data is collected from their medical records. This includes patient characteristics, imaging, treatment and outcome at discharge. There are no follow-up visits.

In a final pilot phase, up to 10 patients per setting will be measured with the AI algorithms built into the EEG recording device, to evaluate feasibility and user-friendliness. In all phases, EEG and algorithm results are not used for clinical decisions.
lead_sponsor: Academisch Medisch Centrum - Universiteit van Amsterdam (AMC-UvA)
primary_outcomes: Prognostic performance of a subhairline EEG-based AI algorithm for neurological outcome prediction in postanoxic coma
Diagnostic accuracy of a subhairline EEG-based AI algorithm for detection of intracerebral hemorrhage
title: AI-based Algorithm Development for Improved Diagnostics in the Intensive Care and Acute Stroke Setting Using Electroencephalography

brief_summary: Brucellosis is a globally distributed zoonosis with persistent clinical management challenges. The World Health Organization (WHO)-recommended doxycycline-rifampin (DOX-RIF) dual regimen may drive rifampin-associated antimicrobial resistance in brucellosis-endemic regions. Patients with osteoarticular brucellosis, the most common focal complication of brucellosis, often require long-term intravenous ceftriaxone triple therapy. This parenteral regimen leads to poor treatment adherence, frequent hospital visits and heavy outpatient burdens. Fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin \[LVX\], moxifloxacin \[MXF\]) exert excellent anti-Brucella activity and superior bone-joint penetration. However, high-quality multicenter prospective data comparing rifampin-sparing LVX-DOX / MXF-DOX regimens against the standard RIF-DOX regimen remain scarce. Existing comparative studies are limited to small single-center retrospective cohorts or trials combining rifampin with fluoroquinolones rather than rifampin-free all-oral triple regimens.

brief_summary:
People having radiation therapy to the head and neck often develop painful mouth problems - mouth sores, dry mouth, mouth pain, trouble eating and drinking, and changes in taste. These problems can become severe enough to interrupt radiation treatment or lead to an emergency room visit or a hospital stay.

This study is testing whether an oral care program called OSEM (Oral Side-Effect Management) reduces how severe those mouth problems become.

Fifty adults starting radiation to a head and neck site at Premier Cancer Center will take part. Each person will be assigned by chance, like a coin toss, to one of two groups:

One group receives the Peace of Mouth Kit - everyday mouth care products including dry mouth candies, ginger candies for nausea, a mouth rinse, a sensitivity toothpaste, a soft toothbrush and a lip balm - together with a short check-in each week with a member of the Premier team right after their radiation treatment.

The other group receives their usual care at Premier, unchanged.

Everyone in the study fills out the same short questionnaire about their mouth each week during radiation, and once more about four weeks after their last treatment. Everyone continues to see their radiation doctor every week, exactly as they would if they were not in the study.

Taking part lasts about 11 weeks in all.

The items in the kit are everyday consumer mouth care products. They are not medicines of any kind, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has not approved them to treat or prevent any disease.
primary_outcomes: Oral symptom burden: area under the weekly oral symptom score curve
title: Oral Care Program for Mouth Side Effects During Head and Neck Radiation Therapy

brief_summary:
Introduction : Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) affects an estimated 14% of French adolescents, with consequences ranging from sleep disorders and academic failure to social and mental health difficulties. Despite growing recognition of the disorder, evidence-based interventions tailored to high-risk youth remain scarce.

Objective : To assess the effect of co-constructed interventions, online (in-game conference and building challenges) and in-person (lecture and campus challenges), on reducing IGD-related risks.

Methods Quasi-experimental comparative study. 200 students (18-25 years) recruited across two gaming schools in Bordeaux and Nantes over an academic year. IGD assessed via the Gaming Addiction Scale at baseline (M0) and 6 months (M6), alongside broader health measures (sleep, mental health, sedentary behavior). Implementation data and qualitative insights are also collected.

Expected outcomes Reduction in IGD scores, evidence on the relative effectiveness of online vs. in-person formats, and actionable insights for scaling school-based gaming disorder prevention programs.
interventions: Online health promotion interventions for gaming school students
In person health promotion interventions for gaming school students
primary_outcomes: Change in Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) score
title: Evaluation of Interventions to Promote Work-Life Balance Among Students at Gaming Schools

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to validate computed inspiratory muscle pressure (cPmus) for monitoring inspiratory effort in adults receiving pressure support ventilation. Researchers will compare cPmus with reference inspiratory muscle pressure calculated using an esophageal balloon catheter, a thin pressure-measuring tube placed in the esophagus. The study will look at how closely the two methods are related and whether they give similar results. Participants will undergo simultaneous monitoring with cPmus and an esophageal balloon catheter. Researchers will adjust pressure support across six levels, recording measurements from both methods at each level.
title: Computed Inspiratory Muscle Pressure to Monitor Inspiratory Effort During Pressure Support Ventilation

brief_summary: The aim of the study is to investigate the effects of respiratory muscle strengthening and diaphragmatic breathing on pain levels, respiratory capacity and sleep quality in participants with shoulder pain and disability.
interventions: respiratory muscle strengthening exercises and diaphragmatic breathing exercises
primary_outcomes: Change in Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI) Score
title: Effects of Respiratory Muscle Strengthening and Diaphragmatic Breathing on Shoulder Pain and Disability

brief_summary: The sample size of this study is 200 participants, aiming to evaluate the protective effect after vaccination with quadrivalent meningococcal polysaccharide vaccine in the 13-15 age group, and to provide scientific evidence and practical guidance for meningococcal vaccination in the adolescent population.
lead_sponsor: Zhejiang Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention
title: Single-center, Open-label Study: Immunogenicity and Safety Observation After Vaccination With ACYW135 Meningococcal Polysaccharide Vaccine in Junior High School Students Aged 13-15 Years

brief_summary: Chronic neck pain is a prevalent musculoskeletal condition that commonly results in persistent pain, reduced cervical range of motion (ROM), functional disability, and decreased quality of life. Instrument-Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization (IASTM) and Post Facilitation Stretch (PFS) are two manual therapy techniques frequently used in physiotherapy practice; however, limited evidence is available comparing their effectiveness in individuals with chronic neck pain. This randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effects of IASTM and PFS on pain intensity, cervical ROM, and neck-related disability. A total of 38 participants aged 18-50 years with non-specific chronic neck pain of at least 12 weeks' duration will be recruited using non-probability purposive sampling and randomly allocated into two equal groups. Group A will receive IASTM, while Group B will receive PFS. Both groups will also receive conventional physiotherapy consisting of hot pack application and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). Treatment will be provided three times per week for two consecutive weeks, totaling six treatment sessions. Outcome measures will include the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) to assess pain intensity, the Cervical Range of Motion (CROM) instrument to measure cervical mobility, and the Neck Disability Index (NDI) to evaluate functional disability. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, after the third treatment session, and at the completion of the intervention period. The study findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of IASTM and PFS in the management of chronic neck pain and assist physiotherapists in selecting the most effective manual therapy approach to improve pain, cervical mobility, and functional outcomes in individuals with chronic neck pain.
title: Effects of Instrument-Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization Versus Post Facilitation Stretch Technique in Chronic Neck Pain

brief_summary: The use of multimodal regional analgesia (scalp block, local scalp infiltration, and sphenopalatine ganglion block) for postoperative pain management after craniotomy
interventions: Group (c): control group patients will receive general anesthesia.
Group (SS): Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block with either Scalp Nerve Block
Group (SL): patients will receive Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block with local wound infiltration
primary_outcomes: The time interval from patient recovery to the first use of rescue analgesia (nalbuphine)
title: Sphenopalatine Ganglion Block Combined With Either Scalp Nerve Block or Local Wound Infiltration for Postoperative Analgesia in Adult Patients Undergoing Craniotomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study was designed to determine the test-retest reliability of the Unsupported Upper Limb Exercise Test (UULEX) in individuals with stroke. Motor impairments following stroke, particularly reductions in upper limb muscle strength, motor control, and functional performance, may adversely affect individuals' activities of daily living and functional independence. Therefore, the assessment of upper limb performance using reliable and feasible methods is important for planning and monitoring the rehabilitation process.

The UULEX is an incremental, performance-based, easy-to-administer, and low-cost field test developed to assess upper limb exercise capacity. Although the UULEX has been used in different clinical populations, evidence regarding its test-retest reliability in individuals with stroke is limited. In this study, the UULEX will be administered twice to individuals with stroke at a predetermined interval, and the consistency between the two measurements will be evaluated to determine its test-retest reliability. It is hypothesized that the UULEX will demonstrate high test-retest reliability in individuals with stroke. The findings of this study are expected to provide evidence regarding the reliability of the UULEX as a clinical assessment tool for evaluating upper limb exercise capacity in individuals with stroke.
primary_outcomes: Test-Retest Reliability of the Unsupported Upper Limb Exercise Test (UULEX)
title: UULEX Reliability in Individuals With Stroke
[Trial of device that is not approved or cleared by the U.S. FDA]

brief_summary: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a common severe complication and a primary cause of mortality following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT).Previous studies have demonstrated that the JAK/STAT signaling pathway exerts anti-GVHD effects by reducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, thereby inhibiting T-cell signaling transduction. Jaktinib is a broad-spectrum kinase inhibitor that targets non-receptor tyrosine Janus-associated kinases (JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and TYK2), as well as FLT3 (FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3) and c-Kit. Preclinical studies indicated that Jaktinib significantly prolonged survival, mitigated weight loss, and improved clinical symptoms of GVHD in a dose-dependent manner in murine models.Based on this rationale, this prospective, single-arm, multicenter, exploratory clinical study was designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Jaktinib in the treatment of Grade II-IV steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD).
title: Jaktinib for Steroid-Refractory Acute Graft-Versus-Host Disease

brief_summary: This Phase 1a, open-label, dose-escalation study evaluates the safety, tolerability, and preliminary antitumor activity of ivonescimab in combination with pemetrexed and platinum-based chemotherapy as first-line treatment for advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma. Ivonescimab is evaluated at sequential dose levels of 3, 10, and 20 mg/kg using a 3+3 dose-escalation design.
title: Safety and Preliminary Antitumor Activity of Ivonescimab Plus Pemetrexed and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Advanced Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma

brief_summary: This is an investigator-initiated, single-center, observational, noninterventional retrospective real-world cohort study evaluating the effectiveness and safety of tarlatamab as second-line or later-line therapy in Chinese adults with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. Clinical data are retrospectively collected from patients who received tarlatamab as part of routine clinical care. The primary outcome is overall objective response rate (ORR). Secondary outcomes include overall disease control rate (DCR) and the incidence and severity of adverse events, including cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). Treatment with tarlatamab and supportive management was determined independently by treating physicians and was not assigned by the study protocol.
title: Real-World Use of Tarlatamab in Chinese Patients With Small-Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about a disease called Friedrich's Ataxia, also known as FA. This is known as an "observational" study, which collects health information about study participants without changing their medical care.

In certain parts of the world, people with FA may not know about the disease or have access to genetic testing to get a diagnosis. To help more people get medical care for FA across the world, researchers need to learn more about any cases that do happen. Participants for this study will come from West Asia, in countries covered by the "Gulf Cooperation Council", also known as the GCC. This will include study sites in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

The main goal of this study is to learn more about the natural history and participant experience of FA in people living in the GCC region of the world. This will include learning about their experiences, symptoms, and how the disease affects their daily lives over time. To do this, researchers will collect information from participants' medical records and regular healthcare visits. Researchers hope that what they learn from this study will help them understand more about FA in this part of the world so that they can better understand people need for their FA.

The main question researchers want to answer in this study is:

• What are the experiences of people with FA, and how does the disease affect people over time in the GCC region of the world?

Researchers will also learn more about:

* About how many cases of FA are happening in this part of the world?
* How different do FA cases look like in this part of the world?
* What information in the participants' medical records helps show the difference between FA and other kinds of ataxia?

This study will be done as follows:

* Participants will join the study after signing an informed consent form, also known as an ICF.
* During the study, health information from the participants' regular visits to their doctor will be collected about every 6 months.
* Information about participants' FA symptoms, medical history, genetic test results, and daily functioning will be collected.
* For participants already receiving treatment for FA, information from before they started treatment may also be collected from medical records.
* During regular visits, researchers will also collect information about participants' FA symptoms and their ability to do their daily living activities.
* Each participant will be in the study for up to about 2 years.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale (mFARS) Score
Change From Baseline in Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Score
Diagnostic Information: Proportion of Participants With Frataxin (FXN) Mutations
title: A Study to Learn More About Friedrich's Ataxia in People Living in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Region of the World

brief_summary: This community-based trial evaluates whether primary care physicians, equipped with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and trained under a standardized protocol with specialist backup, can improve diabetes outcomes through integrated "medication + exercise + diet" interventions. Unlike traditional fingerstick testing, CGM reveals full glycemic variability, enabling personalized, real-time adjustments. The study hypothesizes that this approach will lower HbA1c, reduce hypoglycemia risk, and decrease long-term cardiovascular, endocrine, and immune-related complications. With low-cost, reliable Chinese-made CGM devices, the intervention is safe and scalable. A cost-effectiveness analysis will also assess its public health value.
lead_sponsor: Xiangya Hospital of Central South University
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) <7.0%
Time to First Composite Cardio-Metabolic-Immune Clinical Outcome
title: Preventive Effectiveness of Primary Care Physician-led CGM-supported Comprehensive Intervention on Cardio-metabolic-immune Diseases in Community Patients With Type 2 Diabetes (Community Diabetes Control Project)

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial compared two balanced propofol analgosedation strategies in adults undergoing elective colonoscopy. Participants were randomized to either a standard-dose protocol using an initial propofol dose of 1.0 mg/kg or a structured dose-sparing protocol using an initial propofol dose of 0.5 mg/kg. Both protocols included midazolam and fentanyl. The standard-dose protocol was anesthesiologist-guided, whereas the dose-sparing protocol was administered by a gastroenterologist trained in advanced life support and airway management, with an anesthesia technician present and an anesthesiologist immediately available if required. The primary outcomes were patient satisfaction and clinically relevant respiratory adverse events, with apnea lasting more than 30 seconds as the principal respiratory safety endpoint. Secondary outcomes included propofol exposure, recovery, procedural performance, cardiovascular adverse events, depth of sedation and nociception-related indices, and endoscopist satisfaction.
lead_sponsor: University of Split, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Incidence of clinically relevant respiratory adverse events
title: Dose-sparing Balanced Propofol Sedation in Colonoscopy

brief_summary: Exercise is increasingly recognized as a supportive intervention in oncology and may influence systemic inflammation, immune regulation, physical function, and the tumor microenvironment among patients with non-small cell lung cancer. The EXIMPACT trial will investigate the effects of a supervised aerobic exercise program on immune system- and tumor microenvironment-related biomarkers in patients with NSCLC receiving active immunotherapy. Although immunotherapy has improved outcomes for patients with NSCLC, factors influencing treatment response and strategies to enhance treatment efficacy remain under investigation.
primary_outcomes: Analysis of Serum Biomarkers (Serum CXCL9,CXCL11,CCL2,CCL5,IFN-γ,IL-10 concentration)
Assesment of Absolute CD3+ , CD4+ , CD8+ , CD19+ T-lymphocyte counts, CD16/56+ Natural Killer cells
title: Effects of Supervised Aerobic Exercise on Biomarkers in Patients With nSCLC Receiving Immunotherapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to learn whether consuming grapes during their natural season can help the body adapt to the shorter daylight hours of winter. The study includes men and women aged 30-70 years with either normal weight or overweight or obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does seasonal grape consumption change circulating microRNAs, small molecules involved in regulating gene activity?
* Does grape consumption influence sleep, physical activity, metabolic markers, body composition, muscle function, and gut bacteria during the transition to winter?

Within each population group, researchers will compare participants consuming yogurt with freeze-dried grape powder with participants consuming the same yogurt without grape powder. Both groups will receive the same Mediterranean-style dietary guidance.

Participants will:

* Consume two yogurts daily for 3 weeks, either with or without a total daily dose of 16 grams of freeze-dried grape powder, equivalent to approximately 80 grams of fresh grapes.
* Complete a further 2 weeks of follow-up without the grape intervention.
* Attend an initial information visit and three assessment visits for blood sampling, stool sample collection, and measurements of body composition and muscle function.
* Wear a wrist device to monitor sleep and physical activity.
* Complete questionnaires, dietary records, and a sleep diary.
primary_outcomes: Change in circulating plasma microRNA expression
title: Study of Grape Consumption in Adaptation to Seasonal Photoperiod

brief_summary:
This study investigates changes in the skin and joints of people with psoriasis (PsO) and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) using two non-invasive imaging methods called raster-scan optoacoustic mesoscopy (RSOM) and multispectral optoacoustic tomography (MSOT).

The study will include 192 adults, including people with PsO, people with PsA, people at increased risk of developing these conditions, and healthy participants. RSOM will be used to examine small blood vessels and other features of the skin, while MSOT will be used to examine joints and tissue characteristics. In selected participants, a small skin sample will also be collected for laboratory analysis.

The researchers will investigate relationships between the imaging findings, clinical characteristics, and laboratory findings from skin samples. Computer-based and artificial intelligence (AI)-supported methods will also be used to explore patterns across these different types of data.

The aim is to improve the understanding of changes associated with PsO and PsA and to identify potential imaging features that could be investigated as biomarkers in future studies. The imaging and AI analyses performed in this study are for research purposes only and will not be used to make clinical diagnoses or treatment decisions.
interventions: Skin Biopsy and Skin Sample Collection
primary_outcomes: Association between RSOM parameters and clinical disease severity
