Association between RSOM parameters and histological features of skin biopsies
Association between MSOT parameters and clinical disease severity
Association between MSOT parameters and histological features of skin biopsies
title: Definition of Novel Optoacoustic Biomarkers of Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis

brief_summary: Static stretching, dynamic stretching, elastic (Kinesio) taping, brief cold water immersion and foam rolling are used daily in sport and rehabilitation to prepare the forearm and hand, but it is not known whether, immediately after use, they change how strongly the wrist can flex and how precisely a person can control the force and the position of the wrist. This study measured all five methods in the same 56 healthy adults on separate weekly visits, immediately before and after each method, in a randomised crossover design. Outcomes included peak isometric wrist-flexion force, normalised error in a force-tracking task, normalised error in a position-tracking task, and active range of motion. The study also quantified learning across visits and the measurement properties of the variables. The trial was registered retrospectively; the reason is given in the detailed description.
primary_outcomes: Change in Peak Isometric Wrist-Flexion Force
Change in Normalised Error of the Force-Tracking Task
Change in Normalised Error of the Position-Tracking Task
title: Acute Effects of Stretching, Kinesio Taping, Cold Water Immersion and Foam Rolling on Wrist Strength and Precise Force and Position Control

brief_summary:
Neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy has been established as the standard of care for driver-gene-negative (EGFR/ALK wild-type) stage II-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yielding pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 30-40%. Nevertheless, a substantial proportion of patients (approximately 60-70%) do not attain pCR, and strategies to further augment the pCR rate through treatment escalation remain an unmet clinical need. Accumulating evidence indicates that failure of ctDNA clearance and radiological stable disease (SD) following two cycles of neoadjuvant therapy are each robust predictors of unfavorable pathological response, and their combined assessment may enable accurate identification of the patient subset least likely to derive benefit from immunotherapy.

This single-arm, proof-of-concept study will enroll patients with resectable or borderline resectable, EGFR/ALK wild-type, stage II-IIIB (N2) NSCLC. All participants will initially receive two cycles of a PD-1 inhibitor (nivolumab, pembrolizumab, toripalimab, or tislelizumab) in combination with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy. Following two cycles, patients will undergo ctDNA-MRD assessment and radiological evaluation. Patients in whom ctDNA has not cleared and whose radiological response is stable disease will be assigned to the treatment-escalation group and receive an intensified regimen comprising a PD-1 inhibitor plus anlotinib plus chemotherapy for cycles 3-4, whereas all remaining patients will continue the original regimen. Upon completion of neoadjuvant therapy, patients deemed resectable by a multidisciplinary team (MDT) will proceed to definitive surgery.

The primary endpoint is the pCR rate in the treatment-escalation population. This study seeks to establish a precision escalation strategy guided by ctDNA-MRD in conjunction with imaging response, thereby providing an effective therapeutic approach for patients with NSCLC who respond poorly to immunotherapy and informing the design of subsequent confirmatory trials.
primary_outcomes: Pathological complete response (pCR) rate in the treatment-escalation population
title: MRD and Imaging Guided Adaptive Neoadjuvant Therapy for Resectable NSCLC

brief_summary: This prospective cohort study aims to assess enteral feeding practices and the adequacy of energy and protein delivery among mechanically ventilated children admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit.
primary_outcomes: Number of children achieving adequate energy delivery
title: Enteral Feeding in Mechanically Ventilated Children

brief_summary: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of an 8-week FIFA 11+ warm-up program on selected motor performance parameters in young male soccer players aged 17-18 years. Participants were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (FIFA 11+ program) or the control group (traditional warm-up program). Key motor performance outcomes including sprint performance (10m and 20m), vertical jump (countermovement jump), flexibility (sit-and-reach), static balance (flamingo balance), agility (505 agility), and upper-body explosive power (backward medicine ball throw) were evaluated before and after the 8-week intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Sprint Performance (20-Meter Sprint Test)
title: Effects of FIFA 11+ Warm-Up Program on Motor Performance in Young Soccer Players

brief_summary: The proposed study will test whether magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) can reduce posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms in Veterans. TMS is a noninvasive treatment that uses magnetic pulses to change activity in specific areas of the brain. In this study, MRI will be used to personalize the location of TMS based on brain networks involved in detecting and responding to important or threatening information. Veterans with PTSD will be randomly assigned to receive either active or non-active control TMS over 20 sessions. The study will examine whether active TMS improves PTSD symptoms and changes the brain circuits targeted by treatment. If effective, this approach may help improve and personalize TMS treatment for Veterans with PTSD. This project supports the Department of Veterans Affairs mission of developing more effective, biologically informed treatments for Veterans with PTSD.
interventions: Active MRI-Guided intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS)
Sham MRI-Guided intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS)
lead_sponsor: VA Office of Research and Development
primary_outcomes: Change in Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) Total Severity Score
Change in Anterior Insula Resting-State Functional Connectivity
title: Salience Network Informed rTMS for PTSD

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the immediate effects of acupuncture therapy at three specific acupuncture points (PC6, ST36, and KI3) on intradialytic fatigue in patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing regular hemodialysis. The outcome will be assessed using the Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI) before treatment and two hours after completion of hemodialysis.
title: Manual Acupuncture for Intradialytic Fatigue in CKD Patients

brief_summary: The objective of this study is to evaluate the feasibility of 68Ga-XHER2 PET/CT as a noninvasive imaging approach for assessing HER2 expression in patients with solid tumors and to investigate the correlation between tracer uptake and pathological HER2 expression.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University
primary_outcomes: Evaluate the feasibility of PET/CT imaging with 68Ga-XHER2 for the non-invasive assessment of HER2 expression in various cancer types.
title: 68Ga-XHER2 PET/CT for HER2 Assessment

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial compares two methods of setting positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) during general anesthesia in adults undergoing upper abdominal digestive surgery who are at moderate or high risk of postoperative pulmonary complications.

All participants will receive lung-protective mechanical ventilation. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. In the individualized PEEP group, PEEP will be adjusted to achieve the lowest driving pressure following a lung recruitment maneuver. In the standard PEEP group, PEEP will be fixed at 5 cmH2O.

The main question is whether driving pressure-guided individualized PEEP reduces the proportion of participants who develop one or more postoperative pulmonary complications during the first 7 days after surgery compared with standard PEEP.
title: Driving Pressure-Guided Individualized PEEP Versus Standard PEEP: Effects on Postoperative Pulmonary Complications in Upper Abdominal Digestive Surgery

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the brain activity associated with two common inner experiences: visual mental imagery (mentally seeing objects or actions) and inner speech (experiencing language without speaking out loud). Researchers aim to identify the most effective tasks to generate robust and detectable brain signals (EEG biomarkers) for these experiences in healthy adults. Participants will complete questionnaires and perform specific mental tasks, such as silently repeating words or imagining movements and faces, while their brain activity is recorded using high-density electroencephalography (hdEEG). These tasks will be compared to resting and passive listening conditions to better understand the relationship between inner experiences, self-awareness, and neurophysiology.
interventions: Inner Experience Induction Tasks and hdEEG
primary_outcomes: Modulation of EEG spectral power (Alpha, Beta, and Gamma bands)
title: NEURO-IS: Neurophysiology of Inner Speech Across Neurotypical Participants.

brief_summary:
Chronic nonspecific low back pain is a common musculoskeletal condition that can negatively affect physical function and quality of life. This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effectiveness of visual feedback-assisted sensorimotor training on pain, functional disability, sensory discrimination, and lumbopelvic motor control in patients with chronic nonspecific low back pain.

A total of 70 participants aged 18-65 years will be randomly assigned to two groups: visual feedback-assisted sensorimotor training or conventional exercise therapy. Both groups will receive 12 treatment sessions over four weeks, with three sessions per week.

Participants will be evaluated at baseline, immediately after the four-week intervention, and one month after treatment completion. The primary outcomes will be pain intensity and functional disability. Secondary outcomes will include two-point discrimination, lumbopelvic motor control, fear of movement, pain catastrophizing, quality of life, and disability.

The study aims to determine whether visual feedback-assisted sensorimotor training provides greater improvements than conventional exercise therapy.
lead_sponsor: Sehit Prof. Dr. Ilhan Varank Sancaktepe Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity (Numeric Rating Scale)
Change in Functional Disability (Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire)
title: Visual Feedback-Assisted Sensorimotor Training in Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain

brief_summary: This completed, two-arm randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of therapist-administered myofascial release added to a progressive home-based balance exercise program in individuals diagnosed with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). Forty participants were randomized into a home exercise group and a myofascial therapy group. Both groups followed the same six-week exercise program; the intervention group additionally received myofascial release twice weekly. Thirty-two participants completed the six-week assessment. Static balance, posture, cervical range of motion, muscle strength, and muscle activation were assessed before and after the intervention. The trial is being registered retrospectively after completion of data collection.
title: Effects of Myofascial Release on Postural Balance and Cervical Muscle Function in Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo

brief_summary: The primary objective of study is to investigate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of ETHY-001 in healthy volunteers and participants with Thyroid Eye Disease after single subcutaneous doses.
primary_outcomes: Overall safety profile as assessed by type, frequency, severity and causality of adverse events
title: Evaluation of ETHY-001 for Safety, Tolerability, and Clinical Activity in Thyroid Eye Disease

brief_summary: Cervical stenosis is characterized by a narrowing of the spinal canal that exerts pressure on adjacent sensitive areas, potentially causing significant neck pain and cervicobrachial neuralgia accompanied by functional limitations-conditions that are particularly disabling for athletes. Among the athletic population, anterior cervical discectomy with fusion is the gold-standard surgical treatment. Currently, there is no consensus regarding the timing for a safe return to sports following surgical treatment for cervical stenosis. While various clinical tests are used to assess mobility or pain, no single test specifically evaluates the level of functional recovery.
lead_sponsor: GCS Ramsay Santé pour l'Enseignement et la Recherche
primary_outcomes: Questionnaire Neck Return to Sport after Injury score
title: Evaluation of the Statistical Validity of Cervical Spine Measurements-Including Range of Motion, Strength, and Functional Test Results-for Return to Sport in Patients Who Have Undergone Surgery for Cervical Stenosis and/or Herniation.

brief_summary:
Tennis elbow is a condition that causes pain on the outside of the elbow, typically caused by motions involving straightening of the arm. The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether early surgery leads to better outcomes than physical therapy and watchful waiting for tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) in adults. This study aims to answer the following questions:

* Does earlier surgical intervention improve pain and function more than physical therapy and watchful waiting after one year?
* How do symptoms and function compare between the two treatments over two years?
* How often do people who start with physical therapy and watchful waiting end up needing surgery?

Researchers will compare early surgery to physical therapy and watchful waiting to see which treatment works better.

Participants will...

* be randomly assigned to have surgery or to try physical therapy and watchful waiting.
* have a physical exam and grip strength test at each visit.
* answer questionnaires about their elbow pain and function.
* attend appointments at the start of the study, and at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years.
primary_outcomes: Change in Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE) from baseline to 1 year
title: Comparing Surgical and Nonsurgical Outcomes of Tennis Elbow

brief_summary: This study will compare two treatments for children with beta-thalassemia who need regular blood transfusions and have not responded well to thalidomide. One group will continue thalidomide alone. The other group will receive thalidomide plus danazol and prednisolone. The study will check whether the combination treatment reduces the need for blood transfusions, raises hemoglobin levels, and is safe. About 172 children aged 5 to 15 will be assigned by chance to one of the two groups. They will be followed for 9 to 12 months.
title: Combination Therapy With Danazol, Prednisolone, and Thalidomide for Thalidomide-Refractory Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia

brief_summary:
This study will test a new experimental study drug called REGN9220 with a Regeneron drug called odronextamab (both called "study drug") to see if it can help treat people with aggressive BCNHL that has either come back/gotten worse or has not responded to previous treatment.

The study is looking at:

* What side effects REGN9220 might cause when given with odronextamab
* How well REGN9220 works when given with odronextamab
* How much REGN9220 is in the blood at different times when given with odronextamab
* If the body makes antibodies to REGN9220 when given with odronextamab, this may cause the REGN9220 to not work as well
* How the body and immune system changes after having REGN9220 given with odronextamab, which can help researchers understand why REGN9220 given with odronextamab works better in some people than others
* What is the best dose of REGN9220 when given with odronextamab
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs) during the DLT observation period
title: REGN9220 in Combination With Odronextamab in Adult Participants With Relapsed or Refractory Aggressive B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas (BCNHLs)

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective observational study is to investigate whether oculomotor-pupillary abnormalities detected using a novel edge-AI eye-tracking device can serve as objective and quantitative biomarkers for the early screening and clinical evaluation of Parkinson's disease (PD). The study will include individuals with early-to-moderate PD and healthy controls. The main question it aims to answer is:

Can oculomotor-pupillary abnormalities detected by a novel edge-AI eye-tracking device serve as objective and quantitative biomarkers for the early screening of Parkinson's disease?

Researchers will compare oculomotor-pupillary parameters between participants with PD and healthy controls and evaluate the ability of these parameters to distinguish PD from healthy controls. Participants with PD will also be followed for 12 months to assess longitudinal changes in eye-tracking measures and their associations with clinical changes.

Participants will:

1. Complete standardized eye-tracking tasks to assess oculomotor and pupillary function using the study eye-tracking device.
2. Undergo clinical assessments of motor function, cognitive function, and non-motor symptoms.
3. For participants with PD, attend follow-up assessments over 12 months to evaluate changes in eye-tracking and clinical measures.

The study will also evaluate the feasibility and clinical application of the independently developed edge-AI eye-tracking system and develop and validate lightweight real-time models for PD classification and prediction of disease progression.
primary_outcomes: Differences in mean prosaccade gain between early-to-moderate PD patients and healthy controls.
Differences in antisaccade directional error rate between early-to-moderate PD patients and healthy controls.
Differences in mean prosaccade peak velocity between early-to-moderate PD patients and healthy controls.
title: Oculomotor-Pupillary AI Biomarkers in Parkinson's

brief_summary: This study is testing a new, non-invasive brain stimulation approach for adults with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD). Researchers are evaluating the safety, tolerability, and target engagement of low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) directed at a brain region called the subthalamic nucleus (STN). The ultrasound is delivered using a wearable device called ATTN201 (developed by Attune Neurosciences).
title: SONATA Dose Duration LIFU for OCD

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the impact of cognitive impairment on upper extremity physical performance, cognitive skills, and functional independence in individuals with chronic stroke. A total of 66 chronic stroke survivors will be enrolled and categorized into two groups based on their Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores: the Cognitive Impairment Group (n=33) and the Control Group (n=33). Upper extremity performance, cognitive functions, and functional independence will be comprehensively evaluated using standardized clinical outcome measures.
primary_outcomes: Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT) Performance Time
Functional Independence Measure (FIM) Motor and Cognitive Sub-scores
title: Physical Performance and Cognitive Functions in Patients With Chronic Stroke

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human, open-label, multicenter Phase 1 study of AT-0174, an investigational oral dual TDO2/IDO1 inhibitor. It is being conducted in adults with advanced solid tumors that have progressed on, or are not suitable for, standard therapy. The main goals are to evaluate the safety and tolerability of AT-0174 and to identify a recommended dose for further study.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs)
Number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events
title: Safety and Tolerability of AT-0174 in Adults With Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary: The investigators propose to test the effectiveness of PATH (Peer Advanced Training for total Health) as an educational workforce intervention for improving peer recovery support specialists' (PRSS) overdose prevention (OP) service delivery ability and quality and as a PRSS workforce and service system support. The PATH intervention combines (a) virtual education and (b) case-based consultation. The investigators hypothesize that PATH will improve organizational-level PRSS burnout, additional workforce outcomes, and OP service quality.
interventions: PATH (Peer Advanced Training for total Health)
title: PATH to Reducing Burnout Among Peers Who Deliver Overdose Prevention Services (R33 Phase Clinical Trial)

brief_summary: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-Blind, Multi-Dose, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of LAM-001 (Inhaled Sirolimus) in Adults with Sarcoidosis Associated Pulmonary Hypertension (SAPH)
primary_outcomes: Change in Pulmonary Vascular Resistance (PVR) at 24 weeks
title: LAM-001 for the Treatment of Sarcoidosis Associated Pulmonary Hypertension (SAPH)

brief_summary: Severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count ≤ 50 × 10\^9/L) can significantly increase the risk of bleeding. Safety of Anticoagulation (AC) therapy in cirrhotic patients with portal vein thrombosis (PVT) and severe thrombocytopenia is unknown. Our study aimed to determine safety of AC therapy in cirrhotic PVT patients having platelet counts no less than 30×10\^9/L, especially in those with platelet counts between 30-50×10\^9/L.
conditions: Thrombocytopenia Related to Chronic Liver Disease
title: Safety of Anticoagulation Therapy in Cirrhotic Patients With PVT and Severe Thrombocytopenia

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to compare different therapeutic approaches for the treatment of melasma.

Participants will be randomly allocated into three treatment groups receiving modified Kligman formula, microneedling-assisted topical tranexamic acid, or nanotechnology-based topical tranexamic acid.

The study will compare these treatment approaches over a defined treatment period followed by a follow-up period.

The study will provide evidence regarding the comparative efficacy and safety of these therapeutic modalities in patients with melasma.
primary_outcomes: Change in Melasma Area and Severity Index (MASI) score from baseline to the end of the treatment period
title: New Treatment in Melasma

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to compare two ways of placing and restoring dental implants in adults missing one or more back teeth. The main question it aimed to answer was: does a bone-level implant placed 2 mm below the bone crest, with a final abutment that is never removed, preserve more of the bone around the implant than a tissue-level implant placed at the level of the bone crest?

Each implant was randomly assigned by coin toss to one of the two treatments. Researchers measured the bone level around the implants on dental X-rays at crown placement, 6 months after loading, and at a final visit 12 to 24 months after loading. They also measured two markers of inflammation (IL-1β and MMP-8) in the fluid around the implants 6 months after loading.
interventions: issue-level implant placed at crestal level (Klockner Essential Cone)
Bone-level implant placed 2 mm subcrestally with one-abutment-one-time protocol (Klockner Vega)
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Peri-Implant Marginal Bone Level at Final Follow-up
title: Comparison of Two Dental Implant Types and Placement Depths on Bone Around the Implant in Adults Missing Back Teeth

brief_summary:
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is an autosomal dominant vascular disorder (prevalence approx. 1:5,000-1:8,000) characterized by recurrent epistaxis, mucocutaneous telangiectasias and visceral vascular malformations. Chronic bleeding frequently leads to anemia and iron deficiency, which is associated with restless legs syndrome. Our earlier work suggested that up to 22% of affected patients may suffer from it. Nocturnal epistaxis, nasal clots, and nasal obstruction may further disturb sleep, and positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy may dry out the nasal mucosa, aggravate bleeding, and cause mask intolerance. The association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and HHT has not yet been adequately studied.

This retrospective, exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis aims to determine the frequency of OSA diagnoses documented in the clinical records of our existing HHT cohort. The primary endpoint is this documented frequency, explicitly interpreted as a minimum frequency rather than a true prevalence, since not all patients were systematically screened. Secondary endpoints include details of OSA diagnostics and treatment course, complications of OSA therapy in HHT patients, OSA-related comorbidities (e.g., arterial hypertension, obesity), medication and potential adverse effects (especially respiratory depression), hypoxia-related laboratory parameters (iron status, anemia), and general patient and disease characteristics (sex, weight, height, Curaçao criteria). The findings are intended to inform a possible subsequent prospective screening phase.
title: Prevalence of Obstructive Sleep Apnea in HHT and HHT-specific Challenges in OSA-therapy - a Retrospective Cohort Study

brief_summary: This study compares two different materials used for screw-retained dental implant restorations in the front of the upper jaw (the "esthetic zone"). The goal is to determine which material is better at preserving the bone level around the implant over time and how this will affect the survival rate of the restorations
interventions: PEEK (Polyetheretherketone) screw-retained implant restoration veneered with composite
title: Comparative Assessment of Marginal Bone Loss Around the Implant When Using PEEK With Composite Veneering Versus Monolithic Zirconia Restorations as Implant Restorations

brief_summary: To examined the opportunity for Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents to evaluate transplant candidacy objectively at LT-SC, with a large language models (LLM) representing the expertise of each individual specialist (hepatologist, surgeon, anesthesiologist, psychiatrist and social worker) and coming up with a group consensus decision upon inter-agent communication using prompts GPT-4 in OpenAI (private version).
interventions: evaluate the alignment between AI-SC recommendations and LT-SC decisions
primary_outcomes: Concordance of AI-SC vs LT-SC review
title: AI-SC Multi-center Study

brief_summary: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), which includes deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism (PE), is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality in high-income countries.1 DVT is suspected in pregnancy greater than 10 times more often than it is confirmed.2 The overlap between physiological symptoms of pregnancy (e.g. leg edema and calf, thigh and groin discomfort) and those of DVT often leads to referral for investigation of DVT, especially in later stages of pregnancy. DVT during pregnancy has a strong left leg predominance likely due to left iliac vein compression by the right iliac artery and the gravid uterus.3,4 Unfortunately, the only validated strategies to exclude DVT in pregnant patients require diagnostic imaging as the first step in the diagnostic algorithm. Specifically, compression ultrasonography (CUS), either as a single, whole-leg ultrasound2,5 or as a serial proximal ultrasound6 has been validated to exclude DVT during pregnancy. The LEFt clinical decision score-a simple three-item tool including Left leg symptoms, Edema (≥2 cm calf circumference difference compared to the other leg), and First trimester onset of symptoms-has shown promise in the LEFt derivation study6 and retrospective validation studies.7,8 More recently, the score was tested in a prospective study (LEAD study, OC, ISTH Congress, Paris 2026; submitted for publication), which confirmed its safety in association with D-dimers at the usual cutoff of 500 ng/ml to safely rule out DVT in pregnant patients. However, the diagnostic was quite low as only 7.4% of included patients could have DVT excluded based on this association. When exploring D-dimer at trimester adjusted thresholds of \<500 ng/ml FEUs (1st trimester), \<750 ng/ml FEUs (2nd trimester) and \<1000 ng/ml FEUs (3rd trimester), D-dimer was negative in 142/352 (40.3%) and yielded negative predictive values of 142/142, 100% (95% CI 97.4%-100%). Therefore, we plan a multinational management diagnostic outcome study in pregnant patients with suspected DVT by using 1) an assessment of clinical probability by the LEFt score, 2) trimester-adjusted D-dimer cutoffs, 4) compression ultrasonography.
primary_outcomes: • Symptomatic VTE (proximal DVT, PE, or VTE-related death) during 3 months of follow-up in patients with an unlikely LEFt score (0 or 1) and a negative D-dimer who were not treated with anticoagulant therapy during follow-up.
title: SAFELY RULING OUT DEEP VEIN THROMBOSIS IN PREGNANCY WITH THE LEFt SCORE AND TRIMESTER-ADJUSTED D-DIMER CUTOFFS (the PREG-DVT Study): A PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY.

brief_summary: Falls are one of the most common reasons older adults visit the emergency department. In many older patients, a fall that looks "mechanical" is actually caused by an underlying medical problem such as syncope, heart disease, dehydration or blood clots, and the history is often unreliable. This single-center prospective study will evaluate whether a structured whole-body point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) examination performed at the bedside changes how emergency physicians manage patients aged 65 years and older who come to the emergency department after a ground-level fall. The main question is how often POCUS findings change the physician's working diagnosis, consultation requests, additional tests, procedures, or admission/discharge decisions. Patients will also be followed for one week for death and repeat emergency department visits.
primary_outcomes: Rate of Change in Emergency Department Management After Whole-Body POCUS
title: Whole-Body Point-of-Care Ultrasound in Older Adults Presenting to the Emergency Department After a Fall
[Trial of device that is not approved or cleared by the U.S. FDA]

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a multi-layered digital and pharmacogenomic intervention works to prevent suicide re-attempts in adults with depression. It will also evaluate the safety and effectiveness of continuous digital monitoring, digital safety plans, and precision medication management.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the multi-layered intervention lower the rate of suicide re-attempts over a 6-month period compared to standard care?
* How do digital tools and genetic-guided prescribing affect depressive symptom severity and treatment-emergent adverse drug reactions?

Researchers will compare three groups: participants receiving standard care plus digital monitoring, participants receiving standard care plus digital monitoring and an interactive digital safety plan, and participants receiving standard care plus digital monitoring, a digital safety plan, and pharmacogenetic-guided care.

Participants will:

* Install study smartphone applications (MeMind and eB2 Mindcare) to track daily mood, stress, and activity patterns through active and passive digital phenotyping.
* Authorize historical digital trace extraction via Google Takeout and provide baseline blood samples for genetic, multi-omics, and pharmacokinetic profiling.
* Complete regular clinical checkups and questionnaire assessments at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 24.
interventions: Ecological Momentary Intervention (EMI) via Digital Safety Plan
Pharmacogenetic-Guided Care and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
lead_sponsor: Instituto de Investigación Sanitaria de la Fundación Jiménez Díaz
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Incidence Rate of Prospective Non-Fatal Suicide Re-Attempts
title: Evaluation of a Multi-Layered Digital Phenotyping, Digital Safety Plan, and Pharmacogenomic Intervention for Suicide Prevention in Adults With Depression

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to learn how common medical decisions made during routine care-such as medications, exercise recommendations, referrals, and imaging-affect health outcomes.
lead_sponsor: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
title: Pragmatic Interventions to Advance Cancer Survivor Outcomes

brief_summary:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global public health concern, and the oral microbiome may serve as an important reservoir of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by dysbiosis of the subgingival microbiome and progressive destruction of tooth-supporting tissues. The complex microbial communities within subgingival biofilms may facilitate the exchange of ARGs through horizontal gene transfer (HGT), potentially contributing to the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.

This observational study aims to comparatively investigate the microbial composition, antibiotic resistance gene profiles, and associated mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in the subgingival microbiomes of periodontally healthy individuals and patients with periodontitis using shotgun metagenomic sequencing.

Subgingival plaque samples will be collected from 50 participants, including 25 periodontally healthy individuals and 25 patients diagnosed with periodontitis, attending Istanbul University Faculty of Dentistry. Following microbial DNA extraction, shotgun metagenomic sequencing will be performed to characterize the taxonomic and functional composition of the subgingival microbiome. Bioinformatic analyses will be conducted using established databases and tools, including CARD, RGI, ARGs-OAP, MobileElementFinder, PlasmidFinder, ICEberg, and ISfinder, to identify ARGs, characterize MGEs, and investigate their potential associations.

The study will compare the diversity, abundance, and distribution of ARGs and MGEs between the two groups and assess the potential relationship between periodontal dysbiosis and the genetic capacity for horizontal transfer of antibiotic resistance.

By providing a comprehensive characterization of the subgingival resistome and its associated mobile genetic elements, this study aims to improve understanding of the potential contribution of periodontal disease to antimicrobial resistance and provide scientific evidence supporting the rational use of antibiotics in periodontal care.
primary_outcomes: Richness of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in subgingival plaque
title: Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Periodontitis

brief_summary: Hypoglycemia poses a particular danger for elderly patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). According to data, more than 30% of patients aged 60-69 years experience hypoglycemic episodes, and among persons over 85 years this figure exceeds 50%. The high risk is due to age-related changes: slowing of drug metabolism, decreased renal and hepatic function, weakening of counter-regulatory hormonal reactions, and impaired recognition of warning symptoms of severe hypoglycemia. The consequences of hypoglycemia in old age are especially severe, including increased risk of cardiovascular catastrophes, falls and fractures, and cognitive decline. This study aimed to identify predictors of hypoglycemia and assess its probability in elderly and senile women with T2DM for prevention in clinical practice.
title: Hypoglycemia Risk Assessment in Elderly and Senile Female Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

brief_summary: Capellion is a Phase 2 trial comparing TP-06 2.0% with Vehicle in up to 32 adults with persistent corneal epithelial defects. Participants will receive treatment for 8 weeks and be followed for 2 additional weeks to assess corneal healing and safety.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving complete resolution of corneal fluorescein staining (CFS) in the study eye at day 56, maintained through day 70.
title: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of TP-06 for PCED

brief_summary: This is an open-label extension trial to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of nizubaglustat (AZ-3102) in participants with rare lysosomal disorders who have participated in a previous nizubaglustat trial and wish to continue nizubaglustat treatment.
primary_outcomes: The Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
The Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
title: Long-Term Safety and Tolerability of Nizubaglustat in Participants With Rare Lysosomal Disorders

brief_summary: This study evaluates whether routine urinary catheterization is necessary in patients undergoing laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal (TEP) inguinal hernia repair. Urinary catheters are sometimes used during laparoscopic inguinal hernia surgery to empty the bladder and facilitate surgical dissection. However, catheterization may cause postoperative urinary discomfort, dysuria, and urethral pain. Avoiding routine catheterization may reduce these symptoms without increasing the risk of postoperative urinary retention. In this prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial, 100 patients undergoing laparoscopic TEP inguinal hernia repair were randomly assigned by a lottery-based method to receive either routine urinary catheterization or no urinary catheterization. The primary outcome is the incidence of dysuria on postoperative day 1. Secondary outcomes include urinary or urethral pain, pain severity assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS), postoperative urinary retention, surgical complications, and hernia recurrence. Urinary symptoms and complications are assessed on postoperative days 1, 10, and 30. Hernia recurrence is evaluated during a six-month follow-up period. The study aims to determine whether omitting routine urinary catheterization reduces postoperative urinary symptoms without compromising patient safety.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Dysuria on Postoperative Day 1
title: Urinary Catheterization Versus No Catheterization in Laparoscopic Total Extraperitoneal Inguinal Hernia Repair

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether virtual reality (VR) can be added to routine knee injection appointments at a VA outpatient pain clinic without slowing down or disrupting clinic operations. The study will enroll 45 adult veterans who are scheduled for a knee injection at the Atlanta VA Arcadia pain clinic.

The main questions it aims to answer are

* Can a VR headset be set up and used during a knee injection with minimal time disruptions?
* How many patients agree to take part, how many need to stop using the headset early, and how satisfied are patients and clinicians with the experience?

Researchers will compare patients who wear a VR headset during their injection to patients who receive the usual injection without VR. This will show whether VR may change anxiety, time spent thinking about pain, satisfaction, and memory of the procedure.

Participants will:

* Be assigned by chance to one of two groups. Two out of every three participants will use VR, and one out of every three will receive usual care only.
* If in the VR group, wear a headset showing a virtual environment with little motion. A research team member will place the headset before the needle goes in and remove it after the injection is finished.
* Receive their scheduled knee injection as usual from their clinician.
* Complete a short survey right after the procedure.

Taking part happens during one clinic visit and takes about 30 minutes. The knee injection itself is standard care and is not changed by the study.
primary_outcomes: Willingness to Use Virtual Reality Again
title: Testing the Timing and Application of Virtual Reality Distraction During Knee Injections in a VA Pain Clinic

brief_summary:
This retrospective observational study evaluates whether integrated ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/MR combined with diffusion-relaxation correlation spectrum imaging (DR-CSI) can help predict aggressive pathological features in patients with prostate cancer before radical prostatectomy.

The study includes patients who underwent both ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT and PET/MR before surgery and had complete postoperative pathological information. Imaging features from PET/CT, conventional PET/MR, and DR-CSI are compared with clinical and pathological findings. The main aim is to determine whether PET/MR with DR-CSI can provide additional information for predicting adverse pathological findings after surgery and high postoperative ISUP grade.

This study does not assign participants to any imaging examination or treatment. All analyses are based on previously collected clinical, imaging, and pathological data.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative adverse pathology and its definition
title: Integrated ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/MR Combined With Diffusion-Relaxation Correlation Spectrum Imaging for Preoperative Prediction of Postoperative Adverse Pathology and High ISUP Grade in Prostate Cancer

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effectiveness of the Epley maneuver and the Semont maneuver in reducing dizziness and improving balance in stroke survivors diagnosed with posterior canal benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). Forty participants will be randomly allocated to either intervention or comparator group. Outcomes will be assessed using the Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and Dix-Hallpike test at baseline, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks.
title: Effectiveness of Epley Maneuver Versus Semont Maneuver on Dizziness and Balance in Stroke Survivors With Posterior Canal BPPV

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the performance of NOBO, a yeast-based fermentation product (postbiotic) designed to control axillary odor, in controlling axillary odor in healthy male and female adults age 18 - 70 with confirmed self-perception of body odor. The main question it aims to answer is: Does NOBO decrease self-perceived odor of the intervention axilla compared to the placebo axilla at any time point? Researchers will compare the intervention axilla odor score to the placebo axilla odor score to see if there is a difference in self-perceived odor. Participants will:

* be given a NOBO deodorant spray and a placebo deodorant spray (each assigned to one axilla)
* self assess body odor
* self assess skin irritation
title: A Fifth Proof-of-Concept Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of NOBO, a Novel Postbiotic, in Controlling Axillary Odor in Healthy Adults

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to learn more about genetic factors that may predict if patients with Barrett's Esophagus (BE) will respond to endoscopic treatment. Patients undergoing endoscopic eradication therapy (EET) for their BE may be eligible. After eligibility is confirmed and informed consent is complete, samples and data will be collected for use in this study.
title: Lucid BE Biomarkers Study

brief_summary: The aim is to explain that celiac disease (CD) is an autoimmune, familial disease that develops in genetically predisposed individuals as a result of sensitivity to gluten found in grains and grain products, causing characteristic lesions and malabsorption in the small intestine, and showing clinical improvement with a gluten-free diet. Beyond the gastrointestinal system, the disease affects skeletal muscle health due to malabsorption and malnutrition. Sarcopenia, particularly seen in elderly patients due to decreased muscle mass and strength, can also occur in celiac patients, especially at an early age, due to chronic inflammation, protein malabsorption, and reduced nutrient intake. Therefore, the European Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) recommends regular evaluation of celiac patients in terms of growth, nutritional status, and muscle health. However, gold standard diagnostic methods such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) are insufficient in clinical practice due to high cost, limited accessibility, portability, and radiation exposure, necessitating alternative methods. Ultrasonography has emerged as a promising method for screening and diagnosing sarcopenia in celiac patients. Because non-invasive, inexpensive, and widely available ultrasonography can increase awareness of sarcopenia, enable early nutritional intervention, and improve clinical and laboratory results in celiac disease. The aim of this study is to investigate the evaluation of nutritional status by measuring muscle mass using routine ultrasonography performed on pediatric patients diagnosed with celiac disease in the Pediatric Gastroenterology units of Balıkesir Atatürk City Hospital and Hitit University. Thus, the aim is to determine the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound in the evaluation of sarcopenia in celiac patients.
primary_outcomes: Regional Muscle Thickness Measured by Ultrasonography in Children With Celiac Disease and Healthy Controls
Association Between Ultrasonographic Muscle Thickness and Anthropometric Z-Scores in Children With Celiac Disease
Ultrasonographic Muscle Thickness According to Malnutrition Status in Children With Celiac Disease
Ultrasonographic Muscle Thickness According to Gluten-Free Diet Adherence in Children With Celiac Disease
title: Assessment of Nutritional Status in Celiac Disease Using Muscle Ultrasound in Pediatric Patients.

brief_summary:
Hypernatremic dehydration is a life-threatening condition, particularly in children under two years of age, with mortality rates reaching up to as high as 19%. Infants are highly susceptible due to immature renal function, increased insensible water loss, and limited ability to express thirst. Severe hypernatremia can cause cerebral complications such as brain shrinkage, haemorrhage, seizures, paralysis, and encephalopathy. Furthermore, rapid or improperly managed fluid and electrolyte treatment can increase the risk of cerebral oedema and death.

Although gradual sodium correction is widely recommended for hypernatremia, the optimal rate, route, and type of fluid therapy remain uncertain. Current treatment practices vary and no standardized protocol has been validated in randomized clinical trials for young children. This gap contributes to persistently high mortality and neurological morbidity.

The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether oral rehydration therapy is non-inferior to intravenous fluid therapy in the management of hypernatremic dehydration among children under five years of age with diarrhoea. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does oral rehydration therapy result in mortality rates comparable to those of intravenous fluid therapy among children with hypernatremic dehydration? Does oral rehydration therapy achieve safe correction of serum sodium levels and comparable neurological and clinical outcomes relative to intravenous fluid therapy? Researchers will compare oral rehydration therapy using oral rehydration salt (ORS) solution with intravenous fluid therapy using half-strength acetate in 5% dextrose to determine whether oral therapy is non-inferior to intravenous therapy in reducing mortality and improving clinical outcomes.

Total 268 participants will:

Be randomly assigned to 1:1 to receive either oral rehydration therapy or intravenous fluid therapy.

Receive standardized fluid volumes calculated according to paediatric treatment protocols.

Undergo clinical assessments and laboratory investigations, including serial serum sodium measurements, during hospitalization.

Be monitored for adverse outcomes, including convulsions, fluid overload, and renal impairment.

Have neurological status assessed using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) on admission and at discharge.

Attend follow-up assessments at 1 month and 6 months after discharge for neurodevelopmental evaluation using the Denver Developmental Screening Test II.
lead_sponsor: International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh
primary_outcomes: All-cause mortality from initiation of the intervention until hospital discharge among children under five years of age with hypernatremic dehydration associated with diarrhoea.
title: Hypernatremia Fluid Therapy in Childhood Diarrhoea

brief_summary: This randomized controlled clinical trial evaluated the clinical and biological effects of adjunctive diode laser therapy in the non-surgical treatment of peri-implant mucositis. Adult participants with peri-implant mucositis were allocated to receive either conventional non-surgical mechanical treatment alone or the same treatment combined with adjunctive diode laser therapy. Clinical outcomes included bleeding on probing, plaque index, and probing depth, assessed at baseline and during a 12-month follow-up. Biological outcomes included peri-implant crevicular fluid volume and matrix metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) levels, assessed at baseline and 4-6 weeks after treatment. The implant was considered the experimental unit.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Bleeding on Probing (BOP)
title: Diode Laser Added to Non-Surgical Treatment for Peri-Implant Mucositis

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-blind, randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a telerehabilitation-supported exercise program in women with lipedema. A total of 66 women aged 18 to 65 years with stage I-III lipedema will be included and randomly assigned to either the telerehabilitation group or the home exercise group.

Participants in the telerehabilitation group will perform a supervised exercise program delivered synchronously via Zoom three times per week for 12 weeks. Participants in the control group will perform a similar home-based exercise program independently three times per week for 12 weeks. Both groups will receive education about lipedema and instructions regarding the exercise program.

The primary outcome is pain intensity assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes include pressure pain threshold, lipedema-related symptoms, lower-extremity volume, subcutaneous tissue thickness, body composition, functional capacity, mobility, quality of life, and exercise adherence.
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity Assessed by Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Telerehabilitation-Supported Exercise in Women With Lipedema

brief_summary: Adenoid and adenotonsillar hypertrophy are among the most common causes of nasal obstruction, snoring and sleep-disordered breathing in children, and chronic upper airway obstruction may affect growth, appetite and energy metabolism. Leptin is an adipose tissue-derived hormone that regulates appetite and energy balance. This prospective case-control study aims to compare serum and salivary leptin levels between children with adenoid/adenotonsillar hypertrophy and age- and sex-matched children without adenoid/adenotonsillar hypertrophy, to evaluate the relationship of leptin levels with height, weight and body mass index, and to assess whether salivary leptin, a non-invasive measure, reflects serum leptin levels.
title: Serum and Salivary Leptin Levels in Children With Adenoid/Adenotonsillar Hypertrophy

brief_summary: Brucellosis is a common zoonotic infectious disease. The standard dual regimen of doxycycline combined with rifampicin is widely used for uncomplicated brucellosis. However, treatment failure and relapse still occur in some patients. This study aims to compare the efficacy and safety of two antibiotic regimens in adult patients with uncomplicated brucellosis, to provide clinical evidence for optimal treatment selection.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Shihezi University
primary_outcomes: Clinical and microbiological composite cure rate at Week 6 (end of treatment)
title: Fluoroquinolone-Doxycycline Oral Treatments for Adults With Uncomplicated Brucellosis

brief_summary: In this protocol, the researchers will shift from the past short-term methods to a longer-term deployment and study of a robotic system in a skilled nursing facility setting. The research team will use a repeated baseline-intervention period to understand changes brought on by the robot, specifically. The robot will be deployed in the partnering SNF ambiently (i.e., in a public setting where all residents can elect to use it on demand). Additionally, the researchers will make bi-weekly visits to check in and observe participants performing the intervention activity. The research team will share findings using academic conferences and journals.
primary_outcomes: NNIH Toolbox Motor Battery Pegboard Test
title: NRI: Robot-Assisted Longitudinal Physical and Cognitive Exercise Interventions for Older Veterans

brief_summary:
The purpose of this observational study is to evaluate the effects of Trendelenburg positioning and pneumoperitoneum on mechanical power and respiratory mechanics in adult women undergoing vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) for bilateral tubal ligation.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does Trendelenburg positioning and pneumoperitoneum increase mechanical power during vNOTES surgery?
* How do Trendelenburg positioning and pneumoperitoneum affect respiratory mechanics, including driving pressure, lung compliance, and airway pressures?

Participants who are already scheduled to undergo vNOTES bilateral tubal ligation as part of their routine medical care will receive standard general anesthesia and mechanical ventilation. Researchers will record mechanical power and respiratory parameters at six predefined time points during surgery, before and after the application of pneumoperitoneum and Trendelenburg positioning.

A total of 14 adult women will be included. No additional experimental treatment or intervention will be performed as part of the study.
primary_outcomes: Changes in Intraoperative Mechanical Power During vNOTES Surgery
title: Effects of Trendelenburg Position and Pneumoperitoneum on Mechanical Power and Respiratory Mechanics During V-NOTES Surgery

brief_summary: The present study will evaluate the effectiveness of Buzzy Bee in reducing pain and physiological responses during maxillary buccal infiltration in children aged 5-7 years compared with a conventional injection protocol.
interventions: Intervention A: Buzzy® Bee-Assisted Local Anesthesia
Intervention B: Conventional Local Anesthesia Technique
primary_outcomes: Self-Reported Pain Intensity (Wong-Baker FACES® Pain Rating Scale)
title: Buzzy Bee for Pain and Anxiety Control During Pediatric Dental Local Anesthesia

brief_summary:
This randomized, multicenter, open-label clinical study will evaluate whether adding the Fasten Onco digital therapy, which supports a fasting-mimicking diet (FMD), to standard neoadjuvant treatment can reduce treatment-related fatigue in adult women with stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either standard neoadjuvant treatment alone or standard neoadjuvant treatment together with the Fasten Onco program. Participants assigned to Fasten Onco will follow a short fasting-mimicking diet around treatment cycles, supported by the Fasten Onco digital application and under medical supervision.

The main objective is to compare fatigue between the two groups during neoadjuvant treatment. The study will also assess quality of life, treatment-related side effects, pathological response to treatment, and participants' adherence to and satisfaction with the Fasten Onco program.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in FACIT-Fatigue Total Score
title: Fasten Onco Digital Therapy During Neoadjuvant Treatment for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
Post-ERCP pancreatitis is the most frequent complication of endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP). Rectal non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the current standard prophylaxis. Recent studies suggest that irrigating the papilla with cold water after biliary sphincterotomy may reduce the risk of pancreatitis, but this has not been tested in combination with rectal NSAIDs.

This pilot randomized trial compares rectal NSAIDs plus cold water irrigation of the papilla with rectal NSAIDs alone in adults undergoing ERCP with sphincterotomy. Patients are unaware of their group. The main outcome is the incidence of post-ERCP pancreatitis. Results will be used to estimate event rates and calculate the sample size of a future confirmatory trial.

Unlike previous trials, prophylaxis consists of rectal diclofenac without aggressive intravenous hydration, reflecting standard European practice.
interventions: Cold water irrigation of the papilla
lead_sponsor: University Hospital Virgen de las Nieves
title: Cold Water Papillary Irrigation Plus Rectal NSAIDs vs Rectal NSAIDs Alone for Post-ERCP Pancreatitis (COLD)

brief_summary: Introduction: Type 1 diabetes mellitus is a health condition that produces physical and psychosocial alterations in both the person the person with diabetes mellitus and his or her family, that is why interventions should be designed that make a comprehensive approach to the physiological and psychological aspects of adolescents and parents in order to achieve adaptation to a new normality in the framework of this health condition. Objective: To establish the preliminary efficacy of a comprehensive intervention to promote adaptation in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus and their parents during the transfer of health care responsibility in Bogota, Colombia 2023-2025. Materials and methods: we propose to conduct a pilot study that will develop and evaluate a comprehensive intervention to promote adaptation in adolescents with DM1 and their parents. In the qualitative phase, the needs of adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus and their parents will be explored through focus groups. In the quantitative phase, the intervention will be designed and its feasibility, acceptability and preliminary efficacy will be evaluated. A content analysis will be performed on the qualitative data and descriptive and inferential statistical tools will be used for the quantitative data, considering the behavior of the data. Expected results: It is expected to evaluate the preliminary efficacy of a comprehensive intervention to promote adaptation in adolescents with diabetes.
primary_outcomes: Parental Stress Score Assessed by the Parenting Stress Index-Short Form
title: Comprehensive Intervention to Promote Adjustment in Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes and Their Parents During Transfer of Health Care Responsibility

brief_summary: This study is a single institution non-randomized phase 2 trial looking at the effect of Pulsed Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (PULSAR) followed by neoadjuvant chemotherapy dabrafenib and trametinib (DT) with or without pembrolizumab on patients with advanced anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC). Pembrolizumab will be administered per standard of care (SOC) only to patients who are PDL1 positive at screening.
title: Pulsed Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (PULSAR) With Systematic Therapy for Thyroid Cancer

brief_summary: Mosaic sex chromosome aneuploidy 47,XXY/46,XX is an exceptionally rare variant within the spectrum of Klinefelter syndrome. Available data remain limited, especially regarding adult phenotype and long-term characteristics, and no robust comparative data with non-mosaic 47,XXY Klinefelter syndrome are currently available. This retrospective monocentric comparative study is designed to describe the clinical, biochemical, cytogenetic, gonadal, anthropometric, and socio-professional characteristics of adults with 47,XXY/46,XX mosaicism. In addition, the study is intended to compare these characteristics with those of a homogeneous cohort of individuals with non-mosaic 47,XXY Klinefelter syndrome and with previously published case reports, in order to improve phenotypic characterization of this rare chromosomal condition.
primary_outcomes: Distribution of primary gonadal phenotype in patients with 46,XX/47,XXY mosaicism
title: Clinical, Biochemical, and Cytogenetic Heterogeneity in Mosaic 46,XX/47,XXY Sex Chromosome Aneuploidy

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, multicenter, comparative study evaluating cefepime-zidebactam (FEP-ZID) versus ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) with or without colistin in the treatment of adults with hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP) or ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP). Trial participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either FEP-ZID or CAZ-AVI with or without colistin for 7 to 14 days. Colistin will be added to the CAZ-AVI regimen (or matching saline to the FEP-ZID regimen, to maintain blinding) for participants with a baseline pathogen presumed or confirmed to be CAZ-AVI-resistant. All trial participants will also receive linezolid for coverage of methicillin-resistant staphylococci for at least the first 3 days of treatment.

The primary objectives are to assess 14-day all-cause mortality between treatment groups and to assess the safety and tolerability of FEP-ZID relative to CAZ-AVI with or without colistin. Secondary objectives include 28-day all-cause mortality, clinical and microbiological outcomes at End-of-Treatment (EOT) and Test-of-Cure (TOC), sustained clinical cure at Late Follow-up (LFU), superinfection and new infection rates, and pharmacokinetic (PK) characterization of FEP and ZID.
title: Cefepime-Zidebactam Versus Ceftazidime-Avibactam With or Without Colistin for Hospital-Acquired or Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia

brief_summary: his study aims to evaluate whether adapalene gel is effective and safe for treating acute radiation-induced skin injury in adults receiving radiotherapy. Researchers will compare adapalene gel with Biafine to determine whether adapalene gel reduces radiation-induced skin injury and improves symptoms. The main questions are: Does adapalene gel reduce the severity of acute radiation-induced skin injury compared with Biafine, and what medical problems or adverse events occur in participants using adapalene gel? Participants will apply adapalene gel or Biafine topically every day throughout the course of radiotherapy, visit the clinic every 5 days for examinations and tests, and record their symptoms and any adverse reactions during use.
primary_outcomes: RTOG/EORTC Acute Radiation Morbidity Score for Skin Reactions in the Irradiated Field (Score Range: 0 to 4; Lower Scores Indicate Better Outcome)
title: Adapalene Gel for Acute Radiation-Induced Skin Injury

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if adding PULSAR, a personalized adaptive stereotactic radiotherapy, to standard immunotherapy can control cancer longer in adults with high-risk advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). It will also learn about the safety of this combination. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What percentage of participants are alive without cancer progression 12 months after starting PULSAR?
* What medical problems do participants have after PULSAR with immunotherapy?

There is no comparison group. Results will be compared with published results of immunotherapy alone.

Participants will:

* Continue their usual immunotherapy
* Receive 2 to 3 PULSAR sessions, 3 to 4 weeks apart, with the plan adjusted before each session
* Give blood samples and fill out symptom questionnaires
* Have checkups and scans for up to 3 years
title: PULSAR Radiotherapy Combined With Immunotherapy for High-Risk Advanced Liver Cancer

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate and compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of four different bone regeneration strategies for horizontal alveolar ridge augmentation with simultaneous dental implant placement in the maxillary esthetic zone.

A total of 40 patients with horizontal alveolar ridge deficiency in the anterior maxilla will be randomly allocated into four equal groups (10 patients per group). Group I will receive titanium mesh-guided bone regeneration (GBR) with xenogeneic bone graft, Group II will receive extended sticky bone (ESB), Group III will receive Medpark bone graft, and Group IV will receive Ethoss synthetic bone graft. Dental implants will be placed simultaneously with ridge augmentation in all groups.

Clinical outcomes will include implant stability measured using resonance frequency analysis (Implant Stability Quotient, ISQ) and soft tissue healing assessed using the Landry Healing Index. Radiographic outcomes will include changes in bone volume evaluated using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) before surgery, immediately after surgery, and at six months postoperatively.

The study aims to determine whether these four bone regeneration strategies differ in their ability to achieve bone augmentation, maintain bone volume, support implant stability, and promote favorable soft tissue healin
primary_outcomes: Change in Alveolar Bone Volume From Baseline to 6 Months
title: Four Different Guided Bone Regeneration Strategies for Horizontal Ridge Augmentation in the Maxillary Esthetic Zone With Simultaneous Implant Placement: a Randomized Clinical Trial

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the impact of a sensory-adapted dental environment (SADE) on the stress levels and behavioral responses of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) during dental visits.

Children with ASD often experience sensory sensitivities, making traditional dental care challenging and stressful. In this study, 40 children aged 8 to 12 diagnosed with ASD, along with their parents or legal guardians, will participate in two standard dental visits spaced 30 days apart. The first visit will take place under standard clinical conditions, while the second visit will utilize a sensory-adapted dental environment featuring modified visual elements (such as dark protective glasses), auditory (noise-canceling headphones or relaxing music), taste (unflavored toothpaste), smell (sweet orange essential oil) and tactile adjustments (a weighted blanket).

The study will measure stress using objective tools, including continuous digital biomarkers of stress recorded via wristbands (such as heart rate, electrodermal activity, accelerometer data, actigraphy, movement intensity, step count, metabolic equivalent of task, skin temperature, and peripheral body orientation) and the analysis of salivary lysozyme and cortisol levels in both children and parents. Additionally, standardized psychological questionnaires will be used to assess the child's sensory profile, as well as parental stress and coping strategies. The findings will help determine whether modifying the sensory environment can effectively reduce anxiety and improve the dental care experience for children with autism.
primary_outcomes: Change in Child Electrodermal Activity (EDA) via Wearable Device (Empatica EmbracePlus)
Change in Child Heart Rate (HR) via Wearable Device (Empatica EmbracePlus)
Change in Child Respiration Rate (RR) via Wearable Device (Empatica EmbracePlus)
Change in Child Skin Temperature (ST) via Wearable Device (Empatica EmbracePlus)
Change in Child Actigraphy-Derived Physical Activity Metrics via Wearable Device (Empatica EmbracePlus)
Change in Child Metabolic Equivalent of Task (MET) via Wearable Device (Empatica EmbracePlus)
Change in Child Salivary Lysozyme Levels
Change in Child Salivary Cortisol Levels
title: Adapting the Sensory Environment to Reduce Stress in Children With Autism During Dental Visits

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority trial evaluating whether pelvic drainage can be safely omitted after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). A total of 400 patients undergoing RARP for localized or locally advanced prostate cancer (without planned pelvic lymph node dissection) will be randomized 1:1 intraoperatively - after completion of vesicourethral anastomosis with a negative water-tightness test and satisfactory hemostasis - to either no pelvic drain placement (experimental group) or standard pelvic drain placement (control group). The primary outcome is the overall incidence of Clavien-Dindo grade I-V complications within 90 days postoperatively. The non-inferiority margin is set at 10%. Secondary outcomes include major complications, urine leakage/anastomosis-related events, symptomatic pelvic fluid collection or lymphocele, length of hospital stay, 90-day readmission and re-intervention rates, and urinary continence recovery. The hypothesis is that omitting pelvic drainage is non-inferior to routine drainage with respect to 90-day overall complications, while potentially reducing drain-related discomfort and facilitating postoperative recovery.
primary_outcomes: Overall incidence of Clavien-Dindo grade I-V complications within 90 days postoperatively
title: Non-inferiority Trial Omitting Drainage After Robot-assisted Radical prostatectomY

brief_summary:
Radiotherapy is an important treatment for breast cancer, but it may affect lung function and physical ability, making everyday activities more difficult. Breathing exercises may help women recover after treatment, although more research is needed.

The main aim of this pilot study was to assess whether a four-week respiratory physiotherapy programme was practical and safe for women treated for breast cancer with radiotherapy. The study also explored its potential benefits for lung function, physical ability, physical activity, fatigue and quality of life.

Participants were randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups received patient education and an individualised exercise programme. In addition, one group performed breathing exercises at home using two devices: one to encourage deep breathing (incentive spirometry) and another to provide resistance when breathing out (positive expiratory pressure). The study compared both groups to explore whether adding these breathing exercises provided additional benefits.
interventions: Incentive Spirometry (IS) and Positive Expiratory Pressure (PEP) Training
Individualised Exercise Programme (Aerobic and Resistance Training)
primary_outcomes: Adherence to the Home-Based Exercise Programme
Adverse Events Related to the Intervention (Safety)
title: Multimodal Respiratory Physiotherapy in Women Receiving Radiotherapy for Breast Cancer (RESPIRA-BC)

brief_summary: This is a prospective multicenter, open-label, Phase I clinical study designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of propranolol hydrochloride in combination with adebrelimab and platinum-based chemotherapy in patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC).The study includes two cohorts: patients with previously untreated extensive-stage SCLC and patients with resectable early-stage (T1-2N0M0) SCLC. Propranolol hydrochloride is a beta- adrenergic blocking agent which is associated with augment of immune cell responses. Propranolol hydrochloride may improve the responses of immune checkpoint inhibitors in treating patients with SCLC.
lead_sponsor: Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR) in the Extensive-Stage SCLC Cohort
Disease Control Rate (DCR) in the Extensive-Stage SCLC Cohort
Incidence and Severity of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events in the Extensive-Stage SCLC Cohort
R0 Resection Rate in the Resectable Early-Stage SCLC Cohort
Incidence and Severity of Treatment-Related Adverse Events and Perioperative Complications in the Resectable Early-Stage SCLC Cohort
title: Propranolol Hydrochloride Combined With Adebrelimab and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
Following heart transplantation (HTx), lifelong immunosuppressive treatment is required to prevent the immune system from attacking, damaging, and rejecting the donor hear (allograft). Currently, diagnosis of allograft rejection is based on evaluation of endomyocardial biopsies (EMB), which remains the gold standard for rejection diagnostics. However, previous research have highlighted limitations of EMBs, including interrater variation, sampling error and risks of complications.

Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) has emerged as a promising post-transplant biomarker of allograft rejection. Nevertheless, evidence suggests that dd-cfDNA demonstrates greater diagnostic performance for antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) than for cellular rejection (TCR) and that the specificity exceeds its sensitivity in predicting rejection, highlighting limitations in its clinical application.

The primary objective of this observational project are to investigate if measurement of dd-cfDNA can be utilized as a biomarker for acute rejection in the management of heart transplant recipients during the first year after transplantation in a Danish-Norwegian patient cohort.

Secondary objectives include:

* to correlate dd-cfDNA levels with markers of allograft dysfunction and rejection, i.e., EMBs, ejection fraction, left ventricular global longitudinal strain, troponin T, natriuretic peptide test (proBNP) and score of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV)
* to examine post-transplant dd-cfDNA kinetics during the first 6 six weeks after HTx
* to explore clinical meaningful change in dd-cfDNA associated with acute allograft rejection
* to investigate the association between dd-cfDNA, chronic allograft rejection, allograft dysfunction and patients' long-term survival

To study the objectives, this project will include 100 HTx patients prior to transplantation over a 2-3 year period and conduct a long-time follow up 10 years after transplantation. Patients entering the waiting list for HTx at Rigshospitalet Copenhagen, Denmark, Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet Oslo, Norway, or Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark, are invited to participate in the project. Patients are invited to participate in the current project if fulfilling the pre-defined inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria.

A comprehensive collection of clinical, pathological and immunological data is conducted from up to 15 visits during the first year after transplantation. Thereafter, from all annual visits and upon admission if allograft rejection is suspected.
primary_outcomes: Association between dd-cfDNA level and acute allograft rejection (TCR and AMR) in the first year after transplantation, which will be evaluated using a linear mixed model and reported as the model estimate for the fixed effect (allograft rejection)
title: Donor Derived Cell Free DNA (Dd-cfDNA) as a Biomarker for Allograft Rejection in Heart Transplant Recipients

brief_summary:
This registry aims to investigate treatment options for patients whose previously implanted biological aortic heart valve no longer functions properly. As patients with severe aortic stenosis are increasingly younger and at lower surgical risk, more patients may experience bioprosthetic valve failure during their lifetime.

Treatment options include implanting a new valve inside the existing valve using a catheter-based procedure, surgically removing the failed valve, or providing conservative medical treatment. The study will evaluate outcomes associated with these different treatment strategies to improve understanding of their benefits and risks and help guide future treatment decisions for patients with bioprosthetic valve failure.
interventions: Surgical Explantation of a Failed Transcatheter Heart Valve
lead_sponsor: Institut für Pharmakologie und Präventive Medizin
title: REVIVE-FR Registry

brief_summary: This study is testing the safety and tolerability of a second dose of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine (RSVpreF) given approximately 5 years after the initial dose.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of participants reporting local reactions
Percentage of participants reporting systemic events
Percentage of participants reporting adverse events
Percentage of participants reporting newly diagnosed chronic medical conditions
Percentage of participants reporting serious adverse events
title: A Study to Learn About Revaccination With a Vaccine Called RSVpreF in Older Adults

brief_summary: Traditional medical education methods, which rely heavily on lectures and textbook study, have come under criticism for their inability to foster the critical thinking, clinical reasoning, and practical skills required to manage complex psychiatric cases. The static nature of these methods fails to replicate the dynamic and unpredictable scenarios of real-world clinical practice, thereby hindering students' preparedness for the multifaceted challenges of psychiatric care However, across various disciplines-particularly in medical and allied health sciences-new methods emphasizing active student participation have gained prominence. One such modern approach in health sciences education is scenario-based learning; grounded in situated learning theory, it brings students closer to the professional realities of their field. This method utilizes scenarios as tools for teaching and learning, enabling students to learn from real-world experiences and apply them in practice.
title: Comparing the Effect of Scenario-Based Teaching Method to Conventional Method on Medical Students' Knowledge and Satisfaction in Psychiatry Interns

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to culturally adapt the Perceived Barriers to Exercise Questionnaire (PBEQ) into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties among office workers in Türkiye. The study will use a methodological, cross-sectional design and aims to recruit 300 adults aged 18-64 years who work primarily in a seated, desk-based position.

The adaptation process will include forward translation, synthesis, back-translation, expert panel review, and pilot testing. The Turkish version of the questionnaire will then be evaluated for content validity, structural validity, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, measurement error, and hypothesis-based construct validity. Participants will also complete the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form and the Exercise Benefits/Barriers Scale to assess predefined validity hypotheses.

For test-retest reliability, a subgroup of participants will complete the questionnaire for a second time 10-14 days after the initial assessment. The findings will provide evidence regarding the measurement properties of the Turkish version of the PBEQ for assessing perceived barriers to exercise among office workers.
primary_outcomes: Total Score of the Turkish Version of the Perceived Barriers to Exercise Questionnaire (PBEQ-TR)
title: Turkish Adaptation of the Perceived Barriers to Exercise Questionnaire for Office Workers

brief_summary:
Heart failure (HF) is common among older adults and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Early stages of HF may be asymptomatic or present with nonspecific symptoms, making early detection challenging when screening relies primarily on clinical symptoms. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a biomarker that may help identify individuals with previously unrecognized cardiac dysfunction or HF.
