This study is a prospective, stratified, cluster-randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate an NT-proBNP-driven screening strategy for HF among adults aged 65 years or older in primary care settings. Participating clusters will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either an NT-proBNP-guided HF screening strategy or symptom-based HF screening strategy.

In the NT-proBNP-guided HF screening group, NT-proBNP will be measured in participants, and those with elevated NT-proBNP levels will be referred for further evaluation, including assessment of HF symptoms, echocardiography, to assess HF. In the symptom-based HF screening group, participants with typical symptoms suggestive of HF will be recommended for further evaluation with NT-proBNP testing and echocardiography for HF.

The primary objective is to determine whether an NT-proBNP-guided screening strategy improves the detection rate of newly HF compared with conventional symptom-based HF screening. The study will also compare the HF positive rate and health economic outcomes between the two strategies, as well as adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy among patients with HF.
primary_outcomes: Primary Outcome of Phase 1: New-incident heart-failure diagnosis
Primary Outcome of Extension Study: Composite cardiovascular outcome
title: Screening Elderly Adults in Rural Communities for Heart Failure Using an NT-proBNP-Guided Strategy in China (SEARCH-HF)

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial, titled "Comparison of Extent of Resection of Pituitary Adenoma via Transnasal Transsphenoidal Approach Using Endoscope Versus Microscope," was conducted in the Department of Neurosurgery, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, from 04 December 2022 to 03 December 2023. The objective was to compare the extent of pituitary adenoma resection using endoscopic and microscopic transnasal transsphenoidal surgery. A total of 38 patients aged 20-60 years of either gender were included. Patients with recurrent pituitary tumors or tumors with suprasellar or parasellar extension were excluded. Eligible patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio using random allocation software, and allocation concealment was maintained through sequentially numbered, sealed, opaque envelopes. Group A underwent endoscopic surgery, while Group B underwent microscopic surgery. Preoperative assessment included magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hormonal investigations, perimetry, and routine investigations required for general anesthesia. Tumor volume was calculated using the specified geometrical formula based on tumor dimensions. Both surgical procedures were performed by the same surgical team to maintain consistency. Postoperative MRI was performed six weeks after surgery to assess residual tumor volume and extent of resection. Gross total resection (GTR) was defined as residual tumor volume below 10%, while subtotal resection was defined as residual tumor volume above 10%. The primary outcome was the extent of tumor resection assessed on postoperative MRI. Secondary outcomes included the percentage of tumor resected, tumor volume extracted, and duration of surgery. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25.0. Quantitative variables were compared using the independent-samples t-test, while categorical variables were compared using the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A p-value ≤0.05 was considered statistically significant. Ethical approval was obtained from the institutional ethics committee, and written informed consent was obtained from all participants.
title: Comparison of Extent of Resection of Pituitary Adenoma Via Transnasal Transsphenoidal Approach Using Endoscope Versus Microscope

brief_summary: PERCE-MUCO is a prospective, multicentre, mixed-methods observational study investigating the perceptions, expectations and treatment-change intentions of adults with cystic fibrosis who are currently treated with elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) or whose treatment has been medically discontinued. The study focuses on patients' stated willingness to switch from ETI to vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (VTD), and on the factors associated with this intention, including treatment satisfaction, knowledge and expectations regarding VTD, quality of life, treatment adherence, reported adverse effects, access-related concerns and desired support from an advanced practice nurse. The quantitative component uses a study-specific questionnaire and routine-care CFQ-R 14+ and Morisky-8 data. A qualitative component consists of semi-structured interviews at the Roscoff cystic fibrosis centre.
primary_outcomes: Intention to switch from ETI to VTD
title: PERCE-MUCO: Perceptions and Expectations of People With Cystic Fibrosis Regarding a Change in Treatment

brief_summary: During a waterbirth, blood lost in the pool between the birth of the baby and the mother's exit from the water cannot be collected or measured. At the participating centers, blood loss is measured with a graduated collector bag that is positioned only after the woman leaves the pool, for the delivery of the placenta. The blood loss recorded after a waterbirth may therefore be lower than the true loss. The goal of this observational study, conducted in two Italian hospitals, is to learn whether measured blood loss underestimates true blood loss more after waterbirth than after birth on land. The main question it aims to answer is: Is the difference between blood loss calculated from the drop in hemoglobin and blood loss measured in the collector bag larger in women who give birth in water than in women who give birth on land without water immersion? Researchers will compare three groups of low-risk women with a singleton pregnancy at term: women who give birth in water, women who use water immersion during labor but give birth out of water, and women who do not use water immersion. No intervention is assigned by the study: each woman is classified according to what actually happened during her labor and birth. Data are taken from the clinical record and include hemoglobin at admission in labor and after birth, measured blood loss, and the timing of events in the pool and during the third stage of labor.
interventions: Water immersion during labor and birth
primary_outcomes: Difference between calculated and measured blood loss
title: Measured Versus Hemoglobin-Calculated Postpartum Blood Loss in Waterbirth

brief_summary: TuCAN-Media is a longitudinal study investigating cognitive recovery after stroke in severely affected patients (modified Rankin Scale \[mRS\] score ≥ 3) with large vessel occlusion of the arteria cerebri media/middle cerebral artery (MCA). Cognitive functioning and recovery will be assessed in a comprehensive multi-domain digital-based cognitive testing using the TuCAN-App to facilitate a standardized and rapid testing during the acute phase of a stroke (V2), as well as at 3month(V3)- and 6-month (V4) follow-ups.
primary_outcomes: Group comparision (Rec+ vs. Rec-) of cognitive function between acute stroke and at 3 month follow-up
title: Long-Term Cognitive Recovery After Arteria Cerebri Media Ischemia: A Digital Assessment Using the TuCAN-App

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of a methyl-donor-rich diet during the postpartum period on maternal depression, breastfeeding success, and infant weight.

Postpartum women will first complete a three-day dietary record to assess their intake of selected nutrients involved in one-carbon metabolism, including folate, choline, betaine, methionine, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12. Women whose intake of at least one of these nutrients is below two-thirds of the applicable reference intake and who meet the other eligibility criteria will be eligible to participate.

Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The intervention group will receive an individualized methyl-donor-rich dietary program and nutrition education for two months. The control group will receive standard postpartum care and routine dietary advice.

The study will compare the groups in terms of maternal depressive symptoms, breastfeeding success, and infant weight. Dietary intake will also be assessed.
title: Methyl Donor-Rich Diet in the Postpartum Period

brief_summary: This clinical trial studies whether a chatbot can be used to help collect medical history and perform cancer risk assessment among patients undergoing cancer genetic counseling. With the improved cost of genetic testing and growing utilization of genetics in cancer care and risk assessment, there is growing pressure placed on certified genetic counselors. To address this issue, many have turned to artificial intelligence (the branch of computer science that deals with writing computer programs that can solve problems creatively) for practical solutions to re-distribute the workload of certified genetic counselors. The chatbot in this trial uses artificial intelligence technology to analyze information provided by the patient during a phone call. The chatbot then generates a family history summary, family tree (pedigree), and cancer risk related assessments, which may help redistribute the workload for the certified genetic counselor and ultimately make genetic counseling more accessible. Using a chatbot may be helpful in collecting medical history and determining cancer risk assessment among patients undergoing cancer genetic counseling.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity and specificity of chatbot in determining if patient meets National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) criteria for germline genetic testing
title: Chatbot Utilization for Pedigree Creation and Cancer Risk Assessment in Cancer Genetic Counseling

brief_summary: This randomized platform trial compared ciprofol and propofol for early neurocognitive recovery in adults undergoing painless gastrointestinal endoscopy. The primary outcome was the incidence of delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR) at PACU discharge, assessed via MoCA, DST, SMDT, STT, and Stroop tests (≥ 1 SD decline from baseline in ≥ 2 domains). Secondary outcomes included PACU stay duration, total drug dosage, and adverse events (hypoxemia, hypotension, bradycardia, body movement). Assessments were performed at baseline and before PACU discharge (Modified Aldrete ≥ 9).
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR) at PACU discharge
title: Comparison of the Effects of Ciprofol and Propofol on Cognitive Function After Painless Gastroenteroscopy

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial evaluates the effectiveness of an analog gamification-based interactive narrative intervention (REPRO-QUEST) on enhancing sexual health literacy and behaviors aimed at protecting against sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among female university students.

Participants in the intervention group participate in the REPRO-QUEST interactive narrative game session, while participants in the control group receive standard evidence-based educational material on sexual health and STI prevention (an Educational Booklet). Sexual health literacy and protective behaviors against STIs are assessed at baseline and post-intervention to evaluate the efficacy of gamified learning compared to standard educational materials.
primary_outcomes: Behaviors Aimed at Protecting Against Sexually Transmitted Infections
title: Gamified Interactive Narrative (REPRO-QUEST) on Sexual Health Literacy and Sexually Transmitted Infection Prevention Behaviors

brief_summary: This study is the first time BNT3210 will be tested in people. It will evaluate different dose levels to find suitable doses and to understand how safe the treatment is and how it may help people with advanced solid tumors.
primary_outcomes: Part A only: Occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) during the DLT evaluation period
Occurrence of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) by grade, seriousness, and relatedness
Occurrence of dose interruptions, reductions, and discontinuation of BNT3210 due to TEAEs
Part B only: Objective response rate (ORR)
title: A Clinical Trial to Test if the Investigational Drug BNT3210 is Safe and Potentially Beneficial for People With Advanced Solid Tumors Known to Express the Tumor Marker Sialyl-Tn

brief_summary: Qualitative, longitudinal and single-center study To explore the reproductibility and the acceptability of the sitting position for head and neck cancer patients through their experience of sitting and supine positions in the context of radiation therapy.
interventions: Simulation of radiotherapy session in sitting position
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with setups performed in sitting position for which all interfraction shifts are below 3 mm in all 3 directions and 3 anatomical subregions

brief_summary: Interactions with virtual content can enhance the creation and retention of knowledge. While some studies have found that learning methods involving the body-such as tactile manipulation-can lead to deeper understanding and higher achievement scores, other studies suggest that highly embodied tasks may limit the effectiveness of education by placing excessive cognitive or physical demands on learners. This study aims to compare the effects of different forms of visual representation and interaction (2D, digital 3D, physical 3D) on learning performance, presence, embodiment, and cognitive load among college students.

brief_summary: This study evaluated the effects of a 4-week respiratory muscle training (RMT) program using constant versus incremental threshold resistance on respiratory muscle strength, pulmonary function, extremity strength, and aerobic/anaerobic endurance in trained athletes. Participants were randomized into two groups: the Constant IMT group (trained at a fixed 40% of maximal inspiratory pressure \[MIP\]) and the Incremental IMT group (progressing weekly from 50% to 80% of MIP). Both groups trained twice daily, 5 days per week (2 sets of 30 breaths/day) for 4 weeks. Standardized physiological, spirometric, and athletic performance tests were assessed at baseline and post-intervention.
title: The Effects of Interval Respiratory Muscle Training on Athletic Performance

brief_summary:

The intervention adopts a multilevel socioecological approach, integrating individual, social, environmental, and organisational strategies to support sustainable behaviour change.

The study team will evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and effectiveness of this program in improving sleep and movement behaviours, with anticipated downstream benefits for cardiometabolic health, psychological well-being, and workplace productivity. brief_summary:
Mitochondrial diseases are genetic disorders that affect the body's ability to produce energy. Fatigue is a common symptom that can significantly affect daily activities, physical functioning, and quality of life. This study will evaluate whether modafinil, a medication used to promote wakefulness, can improve fatigue and physical endurance in people with mitochondrial disease. The study will also assess the safety and tolerability of modafinil in this population.

Fatigue prevents patients from engaging in activities necessary to maintain a healthy body and adequate brain stimulation. By treating fatigue, we could improve the quality of life of patients with mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome by promoting better brain stimulation.

15 participants aged 6 to 60 years who have a confirmed diagnosis of mitochondrial disease and clinically significant fatigue will be enrolled. Participants must be able to walk independently for at least 15 meters and meet the other study eligibility criteria.

This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment sequences. One group will receive modafinil first, followed by a placebo, while the other group will receive placebo first, followed by modafinil. Each treatment period will last 7 weeks, with a 1-week washout period between treatments. Modafinil and placebo will be administered orally according to the study dosing schedule. Participants and study investigators /research teams will not know which treatment is being received during each treatment period, only the pharmacy team is unblended and know which study drug vs placebo you are assigned in which group.

The primary outcome measure is the distance walked during the 6-minute walk test, which assesses physical endurance. Secondary outcome measures include walking speed and gait, fatigue severity, the impact of fatigue on daily functioning, and quality of life. Fatigue will be assessed using validated questionnaires appropriate for the participants' age Safety will be evaluated through physical and neurological examinations, blood pressure and heart rate measurements, electrocardiograms, blood tests, and the recording of adverse events.

The treatment period will last approximately 16 weeks per participant, with additional follow-up contact planned for up to 6 months after the participant completes the trial. The study aims to determine whether modafinil improves physical endurance and fatigue in people with mitochondrial disease and to characterize its safety in this population.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Modafinil to Treat Fatigue in People With Mitochondrial Disease.

brief_summary:
Patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis experience a high burden of symptoms, including fatigue, pain, pruritus, muscle cramps, and sleep disturbances, which substantially affect health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Although acupuncture has shown potential benefits for several symptoms in this population, evidence regarding its overall effect on HRQOL remains limited, and the underlying biological mechanisms are not fully understood.

This prospective, randomized, sham-controlled trial will evaluate the effect of a structured acupuncture protocol on HRQOL and symptom burden in patients with ESKD undergoing hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. Participants will be randomized to receive either acupuncture or sham acupuncture in addition to usual care. HRQOL will be assessed using the Kidney Disease Quality of Life 36-item questionnaire (KDQOL-36), while secondary clinical outcomes will assess key dimensions of symptom burden.

The study will also investigate changes in selected neuropeptide and proteomic biomarkers associated with pain modulation, neuroinflammation, and neuroendocrine regulation. By integrating patient-reported clinical outcomes with biomarker assessment, the study aims to explore both the clinical effects of acupuncture and the biological mechanisms potentially underlying these effects in patients with ESKD.
primary_outcomes: Change in health-related quality of life assessed by KDQOL-36 domain scores
title: Acupuncture for Symptom Burden and Quality of Life in Patients With End-Stage Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn whether a program to support sleep and the body's daily rhythms can be delivered safely and consistently to critically ill adults in intensive care units (ICUs). These rhythms help control when people feel awake or sleepy and can become disrupted during critical illness. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can enough participants be enrolled, and can ICU teams consistently deliver the program? Is the program acceptable to participants and care teams? What preliminary effects does the program have on sleep, daily rhythms, delirium (a sudden change in thinking that causes confusion), and recovery?

Researchers will compare the sleep program with usual ICU care. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of these two groups. Findings will help researchers plan a larger trial.

Participants will:

Receive usual ICU care or the sleep program for 7 days, with treatment extended to up to 10 days when appropriate.

If assigned to the sleep program, receive bright light in the morning, tube feeding at scheduled daytime and evening times, daily movement or exercise as their condition allows, and care that reduces unnecessary nighttime interruptions.

Have sleep monitored using a portable recording device and undergo daily assessments for delirium.

Answer questions about sleep and their experience of the study when able. Complete telephone assessments of memory, thinking, and sleep quality approximately 3 and 6 months after enrolment.
title: reALIGNing Circadian Rhythm and Promoting Sleep in the Intensive Care Unit

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational retrospective study is to characterize women with urinary incontinence and to identify factors associated with their response to treatment using artificial intelligence models.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

What are the clinical, functional, and therapeutic characteristics of women with urinary incontinence? Which clinical, functional, and lifestyle factors are associated with response to treatment? Can artificial intelligence models identify patterns and factors associated with treatment response?

Researchers will analyze data from women with urinary incontinence collected during routine clinical care at a specialized pelvic floor clinic. The study will combine clinical information from medical records, measurements obtained from clinical assessment instruments, and daily-life data collected using wearable devices such as activity bracelets. Artificial intelligence and machine learning models will be applied to these data to characterize participants and identify factors associated with treatment response.
interventions: Artificial intelligence clinical decision support model
primary_outcomes: Severity of urinary incontinence (ICIQ-UI SF score)
title: Clinical, Functional, and Therapeutic Characterization of Women With Urinary Incontinence and Analysis of Factors Associated With Treatment Response

brief_summary: Chronic anal fissure is a tear in the lining of the anal canal that can cause pain during and after defecation. This randomized controlled trial will compare topical 0.2% nitroglycerin ointment with lateral internal sphincterotomy in adults with chronic anal fissure. A total of 72 eligible participants will be allocated to one of two treatment groups. The nitroglycerin group will receive topical treatment twice daily for six weeks, while the surgical group will undergo lateral internal sphincterotomy. Participants will be assessed at Day 7 and Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 8. The study will compare the time required for pain relief and complete fissure healing between the two treatment groups.
lead_sponsor: Sheikh Zayed Federal Postgraduate Medical Institute
primary_outcomes: Time to Complete Healing of Chronic Anal Fissure
title: Topical Nitroglycerin Versus Lateral Internal Sphincterotomy for Chronic Anal Fissure
